{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GCku9Lt4qKyTQEYYh7SfvD","type":"tool_result","content":"# Scaffold conventions

Every `arch-scaffold-*` skill follows these. A skill's own file says
what it adds: its input, the files it creates and changes, and the
steps that differ.

## The shape is a file

Every file a scaffold writes has a sibling that shows its shape. In a
tree copied from the scaffold, the sibling is the tree's own file at the
path the skill names. When the tree has no such file, it is the
plugin's copy, `../../scaffold/acme_root/<path>` from the skill's
folder, with `acme` read as the tree's name. Read the sibling, its imports, and
its test before writing. Copy its shape, not its domain. A skill states
only what an agent gets wrong from the files alone.

`<name>` is the tree's name, the folder under `om/src/`. Its forms are
snake case for the package, the logins, and the paths (`free_press`),
kebab case for distributions, cloud resources, and domains
(`free-press`), the upper snake prefix for the environment
(`FREE_PRESS_`), and Title case for prose. Never assume `acme` in a
copy.

## Before writing anything

1. Read `version` in `../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, from the
   skill's folder as `realpath` resolves it, and name it in the output
   as "`<version>`, or a later snapshot of main".
2. Read the sections of `architecture.md` the skill names, then the
   sibling files its steps name.
3. Check every path the skill creates. A file that exists, or a folder
   that holds anything, is a collision: stop and say so, and never
   overwrite. An empty folder is no collision; the skill writes into
   it. A migration stamp already used in its role's folder takes the
   next minute.
4. Ask for everything the input lacks in one message, then proceed.
   When no one answers, as in an unattended run, decide each from the
   product's spec or description and the sibling files, name each
   choice in the output after the files, and go on.

## Names

- A namespace `<ns>` (plural, snake case) has a singular: `<Ns>` in
  CamelCase and `<ns_singular>` in snake case (`orders` gives `Order`
  and `order`). Ask when the singular is not a plain one. Its
  interfaces are `<Ns>ManagerInterface` and `<Ns>StorageInterface`, its
  impls `<Ns>ManagerImpl`, `<Ns>StoragePostgresImpl`, and
  `<Ns>StorageMemoryImpl`, and its getters `get_<ns_singular>_storage()`
  and `get_<ns_singular>_service()`. The field on `Managers` is `<ns>`.
- An entity `<Entity>` has `<entity>` and `<entities>` in snake case.
  Manager operations are `get_<entities>`, `get_<entity>`,
  `create_<entity>`, `update_<entity>` (only on a `Trackable` entity),
  and `delete_<entity>` (only on a `SoftDeletable` one). Storage
  operations are `read_<entities>`, `read_<entity>`, `create_<entity>`,
  and `write_<entity>`, and an append-only record has `append_<entity>`
  in place of the last two. Wire types are `<Entity>View`,
  `Add<Entity>Request`, and `Update<Entity>Request` (only beside
  `update_<entity>`).
- A work kind is upper snake case, and its handler is
  `<Kind>HandlerImpl` (`NOTIFY_SHIPMENT` gives
  `NotifyShipmentHandlerImpl`).
- A cloud resource takes the kebab form of the name. The production
  environment is `production` in every name a process, a role, a
  profile, or a resource reads; only its Terraform folders are `prod/`.

## What the files do not say

Each of these holds in every file a scaffold writes, and each is where
a copy of the shape still goes wrong.

- **The context comes first.** A manager or service operation takes its
  stage first: `ctx: TenantContext` for a tenant, `rctx` on the request
  stage for a transition or the sweep, `ictx` for an identity before a
  tenant, and `octx` on the operator plane. A storage method takes
  `org_id: UUID` first. A method that takes no tenant says why in its
  docstring and is listed under `[tool.arch-check.options.CTX-12]
  tenantless` in the root `pyproject.toml` and in
  `om/tests/unit/test_storage_exceptions.py`. A site that builds a
  stage above the request stage is listed under
  `[tool.arch-check.options.CTX-26] sites` and in
  `om/tests/unit/test_stage_construction.py`.
- **A manager stays within its bound.** `arch-check` refuses a manager
  interface of more than twenty operations (CON-01). A project that
  holds another bound sets `max_operations` under
  `[tool.arch-check.options.CON-01]` in the root `pyproject.toml`. In a
  namespace whose manager delegates, a new operation goes to the
  delegate whose duty it is, and to the manager itself only when no
  delegate's duty covers it, as a transition or the sweep.
- **A delegate takes the operations that are added.** When the
  operations a scaffold adds would take a manager past the bound, they
  go to a new delegate, whose duty is theirs, as `tenancy` has
  `credentials`. The operations the manager already holds stay where
  they are. Moving those, with their callers and their tests, is a
  change of its own, made only when a person asks for it.
- **A delegate's shape.** It is `<Ns><Duty>ManagerInterface` in
  `om/src/<name>/om/<ns>/<duty>.py`, re-exported from the package root,
  and `<Ns><Duty>ManagerImpl` in `impl/<duty>.py`. The root builds it in
  `om/src/<name>/om/root.py` and hands it to the manager, whose
  interface carries it as an attribute, never a method. It has no field
  on `Managers`, and a caller outside the namespace reaches it as
  `managers.<ns>.<duty>`. A delegate that calls a sibling takes it in
  its constructor, typed by its interface, as `members` takes `org`. One
  that needs an operation of the manager, a transition among them, takes
  a narrow callable for that one operation, which the root binds at call
  time, as `org` takes `service_context`. The manager holds the
  delegate, so the delegate never takes the manager.
- **Authorize first.** A mutating manager operation opens with
  `ctx.require(<permission>)`, or `octx.require(...)`, before any read,
  the ones a worker calls included. Only an operation on a stage with no
  permissions (the request stage, the identity stage) and the outbox
  handoff open without one.
- **An update copies onto the stored row.** It reads the row, takes the
  caller's fields less `PROVENANCE_FIELDS` and the entity's
  `MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS`, and builds the copy with
  `model_validate({**current.model_dump(), **changes})`, never
  `model_copy(update=...)` over a dump, which skips validation. Every
  entity declares `MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS`, even when it is empty.
- **The outbox rows ride the write.** A `core`-role write lands its row
  and its `OutboxRow`s in one storage call, and the manager relays them
  at once. A relay that fails is logged and left to the sweep, never
  raised, since the write has committed. Work that follows a write is a
  second row, of kind `work_row_kind(<kind>)`, in the same call, never
  an enqueue the manager makes. A payload, an event, and a socket frame
  carry ids, never a personal field's value.
- **Two fences.** The `org_id` in the query is the fence, and the
  table's row-level security policy is the second. Every table is in
  `TABLE_ROLES` (`om/src/<name>/om/storage/roles.py`) and
  `TABLE_SCOPES` (`storage/scopes.py`), and the migration that creates
  it creates its policy, with `ENABLE` and `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
  Every Postgres statement opens through the base's `_session_for`,
  with the call's scope by keyword. `EMPTY_UUID` is passed only by a
  method on the tenantless list.
- **A backfill lifts the force.** A data migration runs as the
  migration login, which `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` binds, so its
  `UPDATE` would touch nothing. Its SQL lifts the force for the one
  table and puts it back in the same transaction, and raises when the
  rows it touched are not the rows it meant to touch. Its integration
  test seeds two tenants and sees both touched.
- **A cross-tenant case per storage method.** The contract module under
  `om/tests/contracts/` has, for every storage method, a case that
  passes another tenant's id and finds nothing and changes nothing. The
  unit module runs it over memory, the integration module over
  Postgres. Both impls order by the `UUID`, never its string.
- **Two storage impls, one manager impl.** A namespace that fronts an
  outside provider reaches it through a client under `integrations/`,
  with a real impl and a deterministic twin, and the setting that picks
  one.
- **Creates are idempotent.** A route that writes a durable row takes
  the gateway's `Idem` dependency and runs under it, whether it answers
  201 with the row or 202 with the id of work.
- **Every setting is documented and deployed.** A field of a process's
  settings is in `.env.example` under the prefix, and every environment
  under `deployment/terraform/environments/` sets it or wires it as a
  secret. The settings tests hold both.
- **Versions are current.** A library, image, or tool a scaffold adds is
  at its latest stable release that a patch release already follows,
  as Technology Choices and How to Override Them (Versions) states. A
  version the scaffold cannot confirm is named in the output.
- **No placeholder.** No empty module, no `TODO`, no dead import. A
  namespace's `README.md`, and `om/README.md` above it, speak the
  product's language to a reader with no code.

## Changing existing files

A changed file gains an entry: a getter on a root, a field on
`Managers`, a router in `HOSTED`, a row in a map, a member in the
workspace. Nothing is reordered, and nothing is removed but what a
skill's Changed table names as removed.

## After writing

Before the first gate, format what was written with the tree's
formatter, `uv run ruff check --fix .` and then `uv run ruff format .`,
the two the setup target ends with. A formatter run is no gate run,
and no count holds it.

1. Run these, in order, and stop at the first that fails:
   `make infra-up` and `make migrate` when a table was added,
   `make openapi` when a route was added and no step ran it since,
   `make check`, and
   `make migrate-check` when a table was added. The database targets
   run only against the local compose stack, and only when Docker runs
   (`docker info` exits 0). When it does not, they are skipped, and the
   output names each one skipped. A tool runs through the workspace
   (`uv run`, `pnpm run`), never a global install.

   A gate that fails on what the scaffold wrote is fixed, and the
   commands of its step run again from the first: the first run plus at
   most 3 reruns. When the count runs out, stop, and leave the tree as
   the last run left it. A fix edits only files the scaffold created or
   changed.

   Three failures stop at once, with no fix: one that was there before
   the scaffold ran; one of the machine (no network, Docker stopped, a
   port that cannot be moved); and one whose fix takes an exception to
   a rule the guideline states, or removes, skips, or suppresses a
   conformance test. That fix is the person's decision, recorded as an
   ADR.
2. Print the guideline version, then every file created or changed,
   one per line, from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`
   (in a tree with no commit yet, which it lists whole, as the skill
   wrote them), then each command run, once, with the outcome of its
   last run. A stop closes the output with
   `Stopped: <command>: <what went wrong>; <cause>`, the cause one of:
   the count ran out, pre-existing, the machine, needs an exception.

Never commit. A scaffold leaves a working tree for a person to review.

|------|-------|

## Procedure

1. Write the type, the table and its migration, storage, the manager,
   then the wire types and the routes, so each step has what it needs.
2. The migration grants nothing: the role's first migration grants
   every later table by default privilege. A table whose reads all lead
   with `org_id` declares its compound indexes and sets
   `__org_id_index__ = False`, as `files.py` does; a feed's is
   `(org_id, id)`. A unique key on a
   `SoftDeletable` entity is a partial unique index
   `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, and the memory impl refuses a duplicate
   only among the living rows.
3. A create returns `bool`, `False` when the id is already written. With
   a second unique key it returns `InsertOutcome` instead, as
   `create_item` in `om/src/<name>/om/work/storage/` does, and the
   manager reads the row back by the key that collided.
4. Manager operations follow authorize, verify, copy, write, and return
   the copy it wrote. Reads take `Permission.READ`, writes
   `Permission.WRITE`. A `core`-role write carries
   `outbox_row(ctx, "<ns>.<entity>.<created|updated|deleted>", <entity>.id, {})`,
   and a second row when work follows. An `activity`-role entity is
   appended by `append_<entity>` and carries no outbox row. A list is a
   page, `after` and a clamped `limit`, like `get_files`. A get or a
   list leaves out a soft-deleted row, in both impls.
5. On a versioned entity the write is a compare-and-set against the
   caller's expected version, as the orchestrations storage writes
   against `expected_version`. The copy sets `version` to the expected
   version plus one, and a mismatch raises `PreconditionFailed` (412).
   At the edge, the get answers the version as a strong `ETag`,
   `"<version>"`. The `PATCH` takes the expected version from `If-Match`
   or the body's `expected_version`, and refuses a request with neither,
   or with both and different, as `ValidationFailed`. The service impl
   passes the caller's version through and never fills it from the row
   it read, which would make the compare-and-set last writer wins.
6. The service impl translates and never decides. A partial update reads
   the current entity through `get_<entity>`, copies the request's set
   fields onto it (an absent field unchanged, an explicit null cleared
   where the field is optional), and hands the whole entity to
   `update_<entity>`. The create builds the entity with the id the
   `Idem` dependency minted. `delete_<entity>` is a soft delete; the
   hard delete is the sweep's purge, never a route's.
7. The tests hold, beyond one case per operation: for every storage
   method, the case that passes another tenant's id (another person's
   for `both`, another identity's for `identity`); for each unique key,
   a second row refused by both impls; for a named atomic method, two
   callers at once of which exactly one wins, over memory and over
   Postgres; an update sent with another `created_by`, a cleared
   `deleted_at`, or another value of a manager-owned field, which leaves
   each as stored; on a versioned entity, a stale version refused and the
   row left as it stood, and `412` at the edge; and the other tenant
   naming this tenant's row on every route that takes one, answered as
   an id that never existed. The row-level security test reads the scope
   map, so it holds the new table once its scope is declared.
8. After the routes, `make openapi`, so the TypeScript and the Python
   clients carry them, then the screen.

from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.om.base import Platform, new_id, utcnow
from free_journalism.om.community.manager import CommunityManagerInterface
from free_journalism.om.community.storage import CommunityStorageInterface, InsertOutcome
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.community.types.page import FollowPage, ReaderFollowPage
from free_journalism.om.context import IdentityContext, Permission, TenantContext
from free_journalism.om.exceptions import TenantMismatch
from free_journalism.om.journalists import JournalistsManagerInterface
from free_journalism.om.outbox import OutboxRelayInterface
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import visitor_row
from free_journalism.om.tenancy import TenancyManagerInterface


class CommunityOptions(Platform):
    max_limit: int = 200
    purge_batch: int = 1000  # follows one purge statement deletes at most


class CommunityManagerImpl(CommunityManagerInterface):
    def __init__(
        self,
        storage: CommunityStorageInterface,
        journalists: JournalistsManagerInterface,
        tenancy: TenancyManagerInterface,
        relay: OutboxRelayInterface,
        options: CommunityOptions,
    ) -> None:
        self._storage = storage
        self._journalists = journalists
        self._tenancy = tenancy
        self._relay = relay
        self._options = options

    async def create_follow(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID
    ) -> Follow:
        # The identity stage holds no permission of the desk: what bounds the
        # write is that it names the stage's own identity, in the desk named.
        await self._journalists.get_public_journalist(ictx, org_id, journalist_id)
        held = await self._storage.read_follow_of(org_id, journalist_id, ictx.identity_id)
        if held is not None:
            return held
        follow = Follow(
            id=new_id(),
            created_at=utcnow(),
            journalist_id=journalist_id,
            identity_id=ictx.identity_id,
        )
        rows = (visitor_row(ictx, org_id, "community.follow.created", follow.id, {}),)
        outcome = await self._storage.append_follow(org_id, follow, rows)
        if outcome is InsertOutcome.INSERTED:
            await self._relay.relay_all(org_id, rows)
            return follow
        # Two calls at once: the other one's follow is the answer.
        existing = await self._storage.read_follow_of(org_id, journalist_id, ictx.identity_id)
        if existing is None:
            raise TenantMismatch(f"follow {follow.id} is not in {org_id}")
        return existing

    async def get_follows(self, ctx: TenantContext, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> FollowPage:
        ctx.require(Permission.READ)
        limit = max(1, min(limit, self._options.max_limit))
        rows = await self._storage.read_follows(ctx.org_id, after, limit + 1)
        return FollowPage(items=tuple(rows[:limit]), has_more=len(rows) > limit)

    async def get_my_follows(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> ReaderFollowPage:
        limit = max(1, min(limit, self._options.max_limit))
        rows = await self._storage.read_follows_by_identity(ictx.identity_id, after, limit + 1)
        return ReaderFollowPage(items=tuple(rows[:limit]), has_more=len(rows) > limit)

    async def purge_tenant(self, ctx: TenantContext) -> int:
        ctx.require(Permission.WRITE)
        if not await self._tenancy.tenant_expired(ctx):
            return 0
        return await self._storage.purge_tenant(ctx.org_id, self._options.purge_batch)

"""Storage of the community swimlane: the follow rows. Every operation takes
org_id first, but the reader's own read, which takes their identity."""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from enum import StrEnum
from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.community.types.page import ReaderFollow
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import OutboxRow


class InsertOutcome(StrEnum):
    """What a create whose row can collide on two keys did, as the work
    storage's create reports it: the caller reads the existing row back by
    the key that collided."""

    INSERTED = "inserted"
    ID_EXISTS = "id_exists"  # the id is already written; nothing changes
    KEY_EXISTS = "key_exists"  # the reader already follows the journalist


class CommunityStorageInterface(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    async def read_follow(self, org_id: UUID, follow_id: UUID) -> Follow | None:
        """The row as stored; None when the tenant has none."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def read_follow_of(
        self, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID, identity_id: UUID
    ) -> Follow | None:
        """The reader's follow of one journalist of the desk, by its unique key;
        None when they hold none."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def read_follows(self, org_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> list[Follow]:
        """The desk's follows by id, strictly after `after`, at most `limit`."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def read_follows_by_identity(
        self, identity_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[ReaderFollow]:
        """Cross-tenant: one reader's follows across desks by id, strictly after
        `after`, at most `limit`, each with its desk. Takes no tenant: a reader's list
        spans the desks they follow in, so it reads in the system scope, as
        the core reads a person's memberships, and the identity is its only
        predicate (ADR 0087)."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def append_follow(
        self, org_id: UUID, follow: Follow, outbox_rows: tuple[OutboxRow, ...]
    ) -> InsertOutcome:
        """The create: lands the row and the rows that announce it together.
        `ID_EXISTS` when the id is already written, `KEY_EXISTS` when the
        reader already follows the journalist; neither lands anything."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def purge_tenant(self, org_id: UUID, limit: int) -> int:
        """At most `limit` follows of a deleted tenant past its retention;
        returns how many."""
        ...

from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.om.community.storage import CommunityStorageInterface, InsertOutcome
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.community.types.page import ReaderFollow
from free_journalism.om.exceptions import TenantMismatch
from free_journalism.om.outbox.storage import OutboxLandingInterface
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import OutboxRow
from free_journalism.om.storage.impl.memory_base import MemoryStorageBase, MemoryTable


class CommunityStorageMemoryImpl(MemoryStorageBase, CommunityStorageInterface):
    def __init__(self, outbox: OutboxLandingInterface | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(outbox)
        self._follows: MemoryTable[Follow] = {}

    async def read_follow(self, org_id: UUID, follow_id: UUID) -> Follow | None:
        return self._get(self._follows, org_id, follow_id)

    async def read_follow_of(
        self, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID, identity_id: UUID
    ) -> Follow | None:
        return next(
            (
                f
                for f in self._rows(self._follows, org_id)
                if f.journalist_id == journalist_id and f.identity_id == identity_id
            ),
            None,
        )

    async def read_follows(self, org_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> list[Follow]:
        return [f for f in self._rows(self._follows, org_id) if after is None or f.id > after][
            :limit
        ]

    async def read_follows_by_identity(
        self, identity_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[ReaderFollow]:
        return [
            ReaderFollow(org_id=org_id, follow=f)
            for org_id, f in self._rows_across_tenants(self._follows)
            if f.identity_id == identity_id and (after is None or f.id > after)
        ][:limit]

    async def append_follow(
        self, org_id: UUID, follow: Follow, outbox_rows: tuple[OutboxRow, ...]
    ) -> InsertOutcome:
        async with self._lock:
            found = self._follows.get(follow.id)
            if found is not None:
                if found[0] != org_id:
                    raise TenantMismatch(f"follow {follow.id} is not in {org_id}")
                return InsertOutcome.ID_EXISTS
            if await self.read_follow_of(org_id, follow.journalist_id, follow.identity_id):
                return InsertOutcome.KEY_EXISTS
            self._insert(self._follows, org_id, follow, outbox_rows)
            return InsertOutcome.INSERTED

    async def purge_tenant(self, org_id: UUID, limit: int) -> int:
        async with self._lock:
            gone = [f.id for f in self._rows(self._follows, org_id)][:limit]
            for follow_id in gone:
                del self._follows[follow_id]
            return len(gone)

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select

from free_journalism.om.base import EMPTY_UUID
from free_journalism.om.community.storage import CommunityStorageInterface, InsertOutcome
from free_journalism.om.community.storage.tables.follows import Follows
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.community.types.page import ReaderFollow
from free_journalism.om.exceptions import TenantMismatch, UniqueKeyTaken
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import OutboxRow
from free_journalism.om.storage.impl.pg_base import PgStorageBase, delete_batch, deleted
from free_journalism.om.storage.utils.translation import to_model


class CommunityStoragePostgresImpl(PgStorageBase, CommunityStorageInterface):
    async def read_follow(self, org_id: UUID, follow_id: UUID) -> Follow | None:
        stmt = select(Follows).where(Follows.org_id == org_id, Follows.id == follow_id)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            row = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
            return None if row is None else to_model(row, Follow)

    async def read_follow_of(
        self, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID, identity_id: UUID
    ) -> Follow | None:
        stmt = select(Follows).where(
            Follows.org_id == org_id,
            Follows.journalist_id == journalist_id,
            Follows.identity_id == identity_id,
        )
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            row = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
            return None if row is None else to_model(row, Follow)

    async def read_follows(self, org_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> list[Follow]:
        stmt = select(Follows).where(Follows.org_id == org_id)
        if after is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(Follows.id > after)
        stmt = stmt.order_by(Follows.id).limit(limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            return [to_model(row, Follow) for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars()]

    async def read_follows_by_identity(
        self, identity_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[ReaderFollow]:
        stmt = select(Follows).where(Follows.identity_id == identity_id)
        if after is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(Follows.id > after)
        stmt = stmt.order_by(Follows.id).limit(limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=EMPTY_UUID) as session:
            return [
                ReaderFollow(org_id=row.org_id, follow=to_model(row, Follow))
                for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars()
            ]

    async def append_follow(
        self, org_id: UUID, follow: Follow, outbox_rows: tuple[OutboxRow, ...]
    ) -> InsertOutcome:
        # The base reports a taken id as False and names any other unique key
        # it hit; the only other one here is the reader's follow of the
        # journalist, which two calls at once both meet.
        try:
            if await self._insert(Follows, org_id, follow, outbox_rows):
                return InsertOutcome.INSERTED
        except UniqueKeyTaken:
            return InsertOutcome.KEY_EXISTS
        if await self.read_follow(org_id, follow.id) is None:
            raise TenantMismatch(f"follow {follow.id} is not in {org_id}")
        return InsertOutcome.ID_EXISTS

    async def purge_tenant(self, org_id: UUID, limit: int) -> int:
        stmt = delete_batch(Follows, Follows.org_id == org_id, limit=limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            purged = deleted(await session.execute(stmt))
            await session.commit()
            return purged

The manager asks storage for one row more than the page and keeps it out."""

from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.om.base import Platform
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow


class FollowPage(Platform):
    """A desk's followers."""

    items: tuple[Follow, ...]

class ReaderFollow(Platform):

"""The community storage contract. The cases named in `CROSS_TENANT_CASES` are
the tenant fence's evidence: each one presents another tenant's identifier and
asserts that nothing is found and nothing changes."""

from uuid import UUID

import pytest

from free_journalism.om.base import EMPTY_UUID, new_id, utcnow
from free_journalism.om.community.storage import CommunityStorageInterface, InsertOutcome
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.exceptions import TenantMismatch
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import OutboxRow

CROSS_TENANT_CASES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "append_follow",
        "purge_tenant",
        "read_follow",
        "read_follow_of",
        "read_follows",
    }
)
"""Every method of `CommunityStorageInterface` that takes a tenant has a case
in this module that presents another tenant's. The reader's read by identity
takes none; its case presents another reader's identity."""


def make_follow(journalist_id: UUID | None = None, identity_id: UUID | None = None) -> Follow:
    return Follow(
        id=new_id(),
        created_at=utcnow(),
        journalist_id=journalist_id or new_id(),
        identity_id=identity_id or new_id(),
    )


def make_row(org_id: UUID, follow: Follow) -> OutboxRow:
    return OutboxRow(
        id=new_id(),
        created_at=utcnow(),
        org_id=org_id,
        kind="community.follow.created",
        target_id=follow.id,
        payload={},
        actor_id=EMPTY_UUID,
        request_id=new_id(),
        app="api",
    )


async def seed(storage: CommunityStorageInterface, org_id: UUID, follow: Follow) -> Follow:
    outcome = await storage.append_follow(org_id, follow, (make_row(org_id, follow),))
    assert outcome is InsertOutcome.INSERTED
    return follow


class FollowStorageContract:
    @pytest.fixture
    def storage(self) -> CommunityStorageInterface:
        raise NotImplementedError("the concrete test class provides the storage")

    async def test_round_trip_by_id_and_by_reader(self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface) -> None:
        org = new_id()
        follow = await seed(storage, org, make_follow())
        assert await storage.read_follow(org, follow.id) == follow
        assert await storage.read_follow_of(org, follow.journalist_id, follow.identity_id) == follow
        assert await storage.read_follow_of(org, follow.journalist_id, new_id()) is None

    async def test_a_second_create_of_one_id_reports_it_and_changes_nothing(
        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org = new_id()
        follow = await seed(storage, org, make_follow())
        again = follow.model_copy(update={"journalist_id": new_id()})
        outcome = await storage.append_follow(org, again, (make_row(org, again),))
        assert outcome is InsertOutcome.ID_EXISTS
        assert await storage.read_follow(org, follow.id) == follow

    async def test_a_reader_follows_a_journalist_once(
        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org = new_id()
        follow = await seed(storage, org, make_follow())
        second = make_follow(follow.journalist_id, follow.identity_id)
        outcome = await storage.append_follow(org, second, (make_row(org, second),))
        assert outcome is InsertOutcome.KEY_EXISTS
        assert await storage.read_follow(org, second.id) is None
        assert [f.id for f in await storage.read_follows(org, None, 10)] == [follow.id]

    async def test_the_desks_follows_by_id_after_a_cursor(
        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org = new_id()

        assert [f.id for f in await storage.read_follows(org, None, 10)] == made
        assert [f.id for f in await storage.read_follows(org, made[0], 10)] == made[1:]
        assert [f.id for f in await storage.read_follows(org, None, 2)] == made[:2]

    async def test_a_readers_follows_span_desks_and_name_each(
        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        reader = new_id()
        org_a, org_b = new_id(), new_id()
        in_a = await seed(storage, org_a, make_follow(identity_id=reader))
        in_b = await seed(storage, org_b, make_follow(identity_id=reader))
        await seed(storage, org_a, make_follow())
        listed = await storage.read_follows_by_identity(reader, None, 10)
        assert [(r.org_id, r.follow) for r in listed] == [(org_a, in_a), (org_b, in_b)]
        after = await storage.read_follows_by_identity(reader, in_a.id, 10)
        assert [r.follow.id for r in after] == [in_b.id]

        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org = new_id()

        assert await storage.purge_tenant(org, 2) == 2
        assert await storage.purge_tenant(org, 2) == 1
        assert await storage.read_follows(org, None, 10) == []
        assert await storage.purge_tenant(org, 2) == 0

    # The tenant fence, one case per method.

    async def test_reads_are_tenant_scoped(self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface) -> None:
        org_a, org_b = new_id(), new_id()
        follow = await seed(storage, org_a, make_follow())

        assert await storage.read_follow_of(org_b, follow.journalist_id, follow.identity_id) is None

    async def test_another_readers_identity_reads_nothing(

    ) -> None:

        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org_a, org_b = new_id(), new_id()
        follow = await seed(storage, org_a, make_follow())
        assert await storage.purge_tenant(org_b, 10) == 0
        assert await storage.read_follow(org_a, follow.id) == follow

    async def test_create_refuses_another_tenants_id_and_lands_nothing(
        self, storage: CommunityStorageInterface
    ) -> None:
        org_a, org_b = new_id(), new_id()

        assert await storage.read_follow(org_b, follow.id) is None
        assert await storage.read_follow(org_a, follow.id) == follow

async def test_a_reader_follows_a_journalist_and_the_desk_sees_it(
    community: CommunityManagerImpl,
    journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl,
    events: EventStorageMemoryImpl,
) -> None:
    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    reader = visitor()
    follow = await community.create_follow(reader, desk.org_id, journalist.id)
    assert (follow.journalist_id, follow.identity_id) == (journalist.id, reader.identity_id)
    assert (await community.get_follows(desk, None, 10)).items == (follow,)
    announced = [
        e for e in await events.read_after(desk.org_id, 0, 10) if e.kind.startswith("community")
    ]
    assert [(e.kind, e.target_id, e.actor_id, dict(e.payload)) for e in announced] == [
        ("community.follow.created", follow.id, EMPTY_UUID, {})
    ], "the announcement names no one: the reader is no user of the desk"


async def test_a_reader_follows_a_journalist_once(

    reader = visitor()
    first = await community.create_follow(reader, desk.org_id, journalist.id)
    assert await community.create_follow(reader, desk.org_id, journalist.id) == first
    assert len((await community.get_follows(desk, None, 10)).items) == 1

    with pytest.raises(NotFound):
        await community.create_follow(visitor(), desk.org_id, new_id())
    assert (await community.get_follows(desk, None, 10)).items == ()


async def test_a_readers_follows_span_desks_and_are_paged(
    community: CommunityManagerImpl, journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl
) -> None:
    reader = visitor()
    desks = [context(Role.OWNER) for _ in range(3)]
    held = []
    for desk in desks:
        journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
        held.append(
            (desk.org_id, await community.create_follow(reader, desk.org_id, journalist.id))
        )
    first = await community.get_my_follows(reader, None, 50)
    assert [(r.org_id, r.follow) for r in first.items] == held[:2] and first.has_more
    rest = await community.get_my_follows(reader, first.items[-1].follow.id, 50)
    assert [(r.org_id, r.follow) for r in rest.items] == held[2:] and not rest.has_more
    assert (await community.get_my_follows(visitor(), None, 10)).items == ()

async def test_the_sweep_purges_a_desk_only_past_its_retention(
    community: CommunityManagerImpl, journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl, members: Members

    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Managers:
    tenancy: TenancyManagerInterface
    tenancy_operator: TenancyOperatorManagerInterface
    work: WorkManagerInterface
    work_operator: WorkOperatorManagerInterface
    media: MediaManagerInterface
    idempotency: IdempotencyManagerInterface
    events: EventsManagerInterface
    outbox: OutboxRelayInterface
    orchestrations: OrchestrationsManagerInterface
    journalists: JournalistsManagerInterface
    community: CommunityManagerInterface


def build_tenancy(
    storage: TenancyStorageInterface,
    relay: OutboxRelayInterface,
    cache: CacheInterface,
    options: TenancyOptions,
    clock: Callable[[], datetime] = utcnow,
    *,
    identity_provider: IdentityProviderInterface,
) -> TenancyManagerInterface:
    """The tenancy manager with its delegates, each built here and handed to
    it: a caller outside the namespace reaches a delegate through the
    manager, and no impl builds another. A delegate that calls a sibling
    takes it here, by its interface, and one that needs an operation of the
    manager takes that one operation as a callable. `clock` is the one the
    second factor's time step is read from."""
    sign_in = TenancySignInManagerImpl(
        storage, relay, options, clock, identity_provider=identity_provider
    )
    # The account's deletion writes a row under each place its person holds,
    # and a stage comes only from the manager's transition. The manager holds
    # this delegate, so that one edge is bound at call time.
    org = TenancyOrgManagerImpl(
        storage,
        relay,
        options,
        identity_provider=identity_provider,
        service_context=lambda rctx, org_id, user_id: tenancy.service_context(
            rctx, org_id, user_id
        ),
    )
    members = TenancyMembersManagerImpl(
        storage, relay, options, org=org, identity_provider=identity_provider
    )
    credentials = TenancyCredentialsManagerImpl(storage, relay, options)
    tenancy = TenancyManagerImpl(
        storage,
        relay,
        cache,
        options,
        sign_in=sign_in,
        org=org,
        members=members,
        credentials=credentials,
    )
    return tenancy


def build_managers(
    storage: StorageInterface,
    infra: InfraInterface,
    tenancy_options: TenancyOptions | None = None,
    operator_options: TenancyOperatorOptions | None = None,
    integrations: IntegrationsInterface | None = None,
    *,
    media_options: MediaOptions | None = None,
    idempotency_options: IdempotencyOptions | None = None,
    events_options: EventsOptions | None = None,
    work_options: WorkOptions | None = None,
    orchestrations_options: OrchestrationsOptions | None = None,
    journalists_options: JournalistsOptions | None = None,
    community_options: CommunityOptions | None = None,
) -> Managers:
    """`integrations` is the root of the hosted services the managers front:
    the identity provider, which the tenancy manager signs people in and
    invites them through. None is a process that signs nobody in, and every
    call that would reach the provider is refused as unavailable.

    The options after `integrations` are what the process that sweeps sets
    on the managers it purges through: each one's retention and batch. None
    keeps that manager's defaults."""
    # The relay every core-role manager hands its outbox rows to. It reaches
    # the work manager through the root below, because a row of kind
    # `work.<kind>` is enqueued there: the work manager needs the tenancy
    # manager, which needs this relay, so that one edge is bound at call time
    # and the graph the root hands back is still whole.
    outbox = OutboxRelayImpl(
        storage.get_outbox_storage(),
        storage.get_event_storage(),
        infra.get_topics(),
        lambda: managers.work,
    )
    tenancy = build_tenancy(
        storage.get_tenancy_storage(),
        outbox,
        infra.get_cache(CacheScope.REALTIME_TICKET),
        tenancy_options or TenancyOptions(),
        identity_provider=(
            IdentityProviderAbsentImpl()
            if integrations is None
            else integrations.get_identity_provider()
        ),
    )
    events = EventsManagerImpl(
        storage.get_event_storage(), tenancy, events_options or EventsOptions()
    )
    work = WorkManagerImpl(
        storage.get_work_storage(),
        tenancy,
        events,
        infra.get_topics(),
        work_options or WorkOptions(),
    )
    media = MediaManagerImpl(
        storage.get_media_storage(),
        infra.get_buckets(),
        tenancy,
        outbox,
        media_options or MediaOptions(),
    )
    orchestrations = OrchestrationsManagerImpl(
        storage.get_orchestrations_storage(),
        tenancy,
        outbox,
        orchestrations_options or OrchestrationsOptions(),
    )
    journalists = JournalistsManagerImpl(
        storage.get_journalist_storage(),
        tenancy,
        outbox,
        journalists_options or JournalistsOptions(),
    )
    community = CommunityManagerImpl(
        storage.get_community_storage(),
        journalists,
        tenancy,
        outbox,
        community_options or CommunityOptions(),
    )
    idempotency = IdempotencyManagerImpl(
        storage.get_idempotency_storage(), idempotency_options or IdempotencyOptions()
    )
    tenancy_operator = TenancyOperatorManagerImpl(
        storage.get_tenancy_storage(),
        storage.get_event_storage(),
        outbox,
        operator_options or TenancyOperatorOptions(),
    )
    managers = Managers(
        tenancy=tenancy,
        tenancy_operator=tenancy_operator,
        work=work,
        work_operator=WorkOperatorManagerImpl(
            storage.get_work_storage(),
            storage.get_tenancy_storage(),
            storage.get_event_storage(),
            infra.get_topics(),
        ),
        media=media,
        idempotency=idempotency,
        events=events,
        outbox=outbox,
        orchestrations=orchestrations,
        journalists=journalists,
        community=community,
    )
    return managers
# What Free Journalism is made of

This page names the things Free Journalism is made of and says how they relate.
It is written for anyone; you need no code to read it. Each kind of
thing has a page of its own one level down, which says what can happen
to it and which rules always hold. A product built on Free Journalism adds its own
kinds beside these.

## The org and the people in it

An **organization**, org for short, is one tenant: a company, a team, a
household. Everything in Free Journalism belongs to exactly one org, and nothing
in one org can see anything in another. That is a rule, not a choice.

Every person has one **personal org**, made with them the first time
they sign in. It is theirs for as long as they exist, and it goes only
with their account. Every other org is a **team org**, which a person
makes and owns.

An **identity** is one person across every org: the email the sign-in
provider has verified. Free Journalism keeps no password.

A **user** is that person inside one org: the name the org sees.

A **membership** is the user's place in the org, with a role: viewer,
member, admin, or owner. The role decides what the person may do there.

An **invitation** asks a person to join an org, by email, with a role.
The sign-in provider sends the email.

## How a person proves who they are

A **session** is a signed-in visit to one org. It ends when the person
signs out, when it sits idle too long, or when it reaches its lifetime.

An **API key** is a named, expiring credential for a program, with a
role no higher than its maker's. Free Journalism keeps only its fingerprint, so
the key is shown once.

A **socket ticket** is a one-use pass that opens the live channel, the
connection through which changes reach a screen as they happen.

An **operator** is a person on the platform's own allowlist. An
operator works across orgs with an **operator token**: one permission,
an hour at most.

## Journalists

A **journalist** is a profile at a desk: the name readers know the
journalist by. A **desk** is the org a journalist works in, at first the
journalist's personal org; a newsroom is a desk with several
journalists. Readers are not people of the desk: what they do about a
journalist (follow, support, send information) belongs to the desk and
names them, and each of those is free of the others.

## Files

A **file** is a record of something an org keeps in the object store:
its name, type, size, who uploaded it, and why. The bytes live in the
store, never in the record.

## What the platform writes for itself

No person creates these and no screen shows them, but each belongs to
an org like everything else.

An **event** is a line in the org's diary: what changed, how, by whom,
and when. The lines are numbered with no gaps. An **audit entry** is an
event the platform records about itself, such as a job that failed for
good.

An **outbox row** is a note written in the same stroke as a change,
saying "tell everyone about this". The event and the live push come
from it, so no change goes unannounced.

A **work item** is a job for later. It waits in a queue until a worker
claims it, holds it for a short lease, and does it.

An **orchestration** is a long job kept as a record, done one step at a
time. It succeeds, fails, or parks until what it waits for is back.

An **idempotency record** remembers the outcome of a request that may
arrive twice, so the second copy gets the first one's answer.

## How they fit together

- An org has users. A user is one identity's place in the org, held by
  a membership with a role.
- A desk has journalists. A journalist belongs to exactly one desk, and
  another desk's journalist is one that does not exist.
- A session or an API key belongs to a user, so everything done with
  it is done as that user in that org.
- Every change a screen acts on writes an outbox row, which becomes an
  event in the org's diary, which reaches every open screen of the org.
- A work item, an orchestration, an idempotency record, an event, and
  an outbox row each name their org, so the fence between orgs holds
  for them too.

"""The payments provider: the hosted service that takes a reader's money.
Free Journalism sends the reader's browser to the provider's own page with
an amount, a currency, and whether it is once or monthly; no card number
reaches the platform. The provider's word on what was paid comes back as a
signed delivery, never on the browser's (ADR 0083).

One interface, a real client (`stripe.py`), a deterministic twin
(`twin.py`), and the absent provider (`absent.py`) of a process that takes
no money, such as the worker.

A checkout carries the support's id as its reference and the desk's org id,
and every delivery about it names both again, so the worker applies it
under the org it names. A call a request makes carries the request's
`deadline` (ADR 0069), and ends by then, `ProviderUnavailable`, as when the
provider does not answer."""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from datetime import datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class _Frozen(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)


class Cadence(StrEnum):
    """How often a support is charged: once, or every month until it ends."""

    ONE_TIME = "one_time"
    MONTHLY = "monthly"


class CheckoutRequest(_Frozen):
    """A checkout to open. `reference` is the support's id, which the
    provider keeps and hands back on every delivery about the checkout, and
    `org_id` the desk it is for. Amounts are in the currency's minor units
    (cents); `currency` is its ISO 4217 code in lower case. `application_fee`
    is the platform's fee out of `amount`, apart from the processor's."""

    reference: UUID
    org_id: UUID
    amount: int = Field(gt=0)
    currency: str = Field(pattern=r"^[a-z]{3}$")
    cadence: Cadence
    application_fee: int = Field(ge=0)
    success_url: str
    cancel_url: str


class Checkout(_Frozen):
    """An opened checkout: the provider's id for it, and where the reader's
    browser goes to pay."""

    id: str
    url: str


class PaymentOutcome(StrEnum):
    """What a delivery says became of a checkout."""

    PAID = "paid"
    """A one-time checkout is paid."""
    ACTIVE = "active"
    """A monthly checkout is paid, and its subscription runs."""
    FAILED = "failed"
    """The payment failed after the reader left the page."""
    EXPIRED = "expired"
    """The checkout lapsed unpaid."""


class PaymentDelivery(_Frozen):
    """One event the provider delivered to the webhook route, once its
    signature checked out. `key` is the delivery's key, the same for every
    copy of the event. `org_id` and `reference` are the desk and the support
    the checkout was opened for, read from its metadata, and None when the
    event carries none that parses. `outcome` is None for an event the
    product does not act on."""

    key: UUID
    event_id: str
    event_type: str
    created: datetime
    org_id: UUID | None = None
    reference: UUID | None = None
    checkout_id: str | None = None
    outcome: PaymentOutcome | None = None


class PaymentsProviderInterface(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def configured(self) -> bool:
        """False when this process cannot open a checkout through it."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def open_checkout(
        self, request: CheckoutRequest, *, deadline: datetime | None = None
    ) -> Checkout:
        """Opens a checkout on the provider's hosted page: a one-time payment,
        or a monthly subscription. The reader comes back to `success_url` or
        `cancel_url`, which say nothing of what was paid; the delivery does.
        ProviderRefused when the provider refuses what it was handed."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def verify_delivery(self, payload: bytes, signature: str) -> PaymentDelivery:
        """The event a webhook delivery carries, once the signature over its
        body and its timestamp checks out under the endpoint's secret;
        `DeliveryRefused` otherwise, and `ProviderUnavailable` when this
        process holds no secret. It makes no call."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def describe(self) -> str: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def start(self) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def close(self) -> None: ...
"""The payments provider's twin: deterministic, in-process, and for a local
environment only (the configured root refuses it anywhere else). It keeps
every checkout it opened in memory, with the request it was opened for.

A test or a local process drives the reader's and the provider's side
through the twin's own methods: `complete` stands for a reader paying on the
hosted page, `expire` for a checkout left to lapse, and `signed_event` for
any other event about a checkout. Each answers the delivery the provider
would send, the body and its `Stripe-Signature` header, signed with the
twin's webhook secret, for the test to post to the webhook route. Every id
it mints says it is the twin's (`twin_`), so a row that holds one names its
provenance."""

import itertools
import json
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from free_journalism.integrations.payments import (
    Cadence,
    Checkout,
    CheckoutRequest,
    PaymentDelivery,
    PaymentsProviderInterface,
)
from free_journalism.integrations.payments.deliveries import (
    COMPLETED,
    EXPIRED,
    sign,
    verified,
)

TWIN_CHECKOUT = "https://checkout.twin.test"
TWIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET = "twin-payments-webhook-secret"
"""The secret the twin signs its deliveries with by default; never a real
endpoint's."""


class PaymentsProviderTwinImpl(PaymentsProviderInterface):
    def __init__(
        self, *, webhook_secret: str = TWIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET, clock: type[datetime] = datetime
    ) -> None:
        self._counter = itertools.count(1)
        self._secret = webhook_secret
        self._clock = clock
        self.checkouts: dict[str, CheckoutRequest] = {}
        """Every checkout the twin opened, by id, in order, with its request."""

    def _id(self, kind: str) -> str:
        return f"twin_{kind}_{next(self._counter):06d}"

    # The reader's and the provider's side, driven by a test or a local process.

    def complete(self, checkout_id: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
        """The reader paid: the delivery of the completed checkout, paid, a
        payment for a one-time checkout and a running subscription for a
        monthly one."""
        return self.signed_event(COMPLETED, checkout_id)

    def expire(self, checkout_id: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
        """The checkout lapsed unpaid: the delivery that says so."""
        return self.signed_event(EXPIRED, checkout_id)

    def signed_event(
        self, event_type: str, checkout_id: str, event_id: str | None = None
    ) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
        """An event about a checkout the twin opened, as the provider would
        deliver it: the body, in the provider's shape, and the signature
        header over it. The same `event_id` is the same delivery. KeyError
        for a checkout the twin never opened."""
        request = self.checkouts[checkout_id]
        monthly = request.cadence is Cadence.MONTHLY
        expired = event_type == EXPIRED
        session = {
            "id": checkout_id,
            "object": "checkout.session",
            "mode": "subscription" if monthly else "payment",
            "status": "expired" if expired else "complete",
            "payment_status": "paid" if event_type == COMPLETED else "unpaid",
            "amount_total": request.amount,
            "currency": request.currency,
            "client_reference_id": str(request.reference),
            "metadata": {"support_id": str(request.reference), "org_id": str(request.org_id)},
            "url": None,
        }
        event = {
            "id": event_id or self._id("evt"),
            "object": "event",
            "type": event_type,
            "created": int(self._clock.now(UTC).timestamp()),
            "livemode": False,
            "data": {"object": session},
        }
        payload = json.dumps(event).encode()
        return payload, sign(payload, self._secret)

    # The interface.

    @property
    def configured(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def open_checkout(
        self, request: CheckoutRequest, *, deadline: datetime | None = None
    ) -> Checkout:
        checkout_id = self._id("cs")
        self.checkouts[checkout_id] = request
        return Checkout(id=checkout_id, url=f"{TWIN_CHECKOUT}/{checkout_id}")

    def verify_delivery(self, payload: bytes, signature: str) -> PaymentDelivery:
        return verified(payload, signature, self._secret)

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return "payments provider: the twin (in-process, local only)"

    async def start(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None
"""The provider of a process whose environment names none: every call is
refused as unavailable, and no money is taken."""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import NoReturn

from free_journalism.integrations.exceptions import ProviderUnavailable
from free_journalism.integrations.payments import (
    Checkout,
    CheckoutRequest,
    PaymentDelivery,
    PaymentsProviderInterface,
)


class PaymentsProviderAbsentImpl(PaymentsProviderInterface):
    def __init__(self, reason: str = "no payments provider is configured") -> None:
        self._reason = reason

    def _refuse(self) -> NoReturn:
        raise ProviderUnavailable(self._reason)

    @property
    def configured(self) -> bool:
        return False

    async def open_checkout(
        self, request: CheckoutRequest, *, deadline: datetime | None = None
    ) -> Checkout:
        self._refuse()

    def verify_delivery(self, payload: bytes, signature: str) -> PaymentDelivery:
        self._refuse()

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return f"payments provider: none ({self._reason})"

    async def start(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

A source who wants replies has their device make a follow-up secret (the platform keeps only its SHA-256 hex digest) and an X25519 key pair whose public half rides on the delivery so a journalist's reply is encrypted to it; a source's messages are encrypted to the journalist's public key. # ADR 0082: Free Journalism on the core: a journalist's desk is an org

**Status**: accepted (2026-09-30)

## Context

Free Journalism is a platform for supporting independent journalists
directly and for giving communities a safe channel to bring them
information. Its first release proves three loops: people follow and
financially support journalists; people send useful local information to
journalists; journalists use their inbox and write back.

The core it is built on holds tenancy with an operator plane, events and
audit, the outbox, idempotency, the work queue, orchestrations, and
files. Every row belongs to one org, and nothing in one org sees another
(The Second Fence). The product has to say what its people and places
are in those terms before its first namespace lands, since every table
after it is fenced by the answer.

Three facts of the product constrain the answer. A reader follows and
supports many journalists, each in their own place. A source may send
information with no account at all. A report is encrypted on the
sender's device for each recipient journalist, and the platform never
holds its plaintext or a journalist's private key.

## Decision

**An org is a journalist's desk.** A journalist's profile, their
updates, their inbox, their notes, their investigations, and the support
paid to them belong to the org the journalist works in. At first that is
the journalist's personal org, which the core makes at the first
sign-in. A newsroom, a team org holding several journalists, is outside
the first release, and nothing here rules it out: an org may hold more
than one journalist profile.

**A member is a person who works a desk.** The journalist is the owner
of their org. An assistant or an editor a journalist invites later is a
member with the core's role ladder. A reader is never a member of a
journalist's org.

**A reader is an identity, and their follows and support are the
journalist's rows.** A follow and a support payment land in the
journalist's org, naming the reader's identity. The journalist reads
them by org; the reader reads their own across desks through the
identity scope the core already fences (`ScopeKind.IDENTITY`), never by
reading another org. A reader's personal org holds only what is theirs
alone: their notification settings and their notification centre.

**A source is not an identity.** A report is sent through a public
route that takes no account. Each recipient journalist's org gets a
delivery row: its own wrapped copy of the report key and a reference to
the one ciphertext. The ciphertext is kept once, in the object store,
under a key no org owns, and removed when the last delivery that names
it is purged. A source who wants replies holds a follow-up secret their
device made; the platform keeps only its digest. The source's contact
method, if they give one, is encrypted to the recipients like the
report, so the platform keeps no source identity in the clear. Logs,
events, and telemetry of a source route carry no address, no user agent,
and no identifier of the sender.

**The platform never decrypts a report.** What the platform cannot read
it cannot process: metadata stripping (a photo's EXIF) and the choice of
what to send are the sender's client's, before encryption. The malware
check of an attachment of a report is the recipient's client's, by the
attachment's digest ([ADR 0086](0086-the-malware-scanner.md)). A report
becomes public only by a journalist's editorial action, which publishes
something new under the journalist's name; the report itself stays
private.

**An operator is the platform's trust and safety staff.** Journalist
verification, abuse and threat reports, blocks, and the retention of
sensitive submissions are worked on the operator plane, through
`/v1/admin/*` with an operator token
([ADR 0010](0010-operators-work-through-the-api.md)). An operator never
reads a report's contents, which the platform cannot decrypt, and every
journalist-side open of a report is an audit entry in the desk's stream.

**The core's pieces the product uses:**

| Piece | Used for |
|-------|----------|
| Tenancy | desks as orgs, readers and journalists as identities, sign-in through WorkOS AuthKit ([ADR 0028](0028-sign-in-is-the-identity-providers.md)) |
| Files | profile pictures and the media of a journalist's updates, which the platform sees; the ciphertext of a report and its attachments, which it does not |
| Orchestrations | a journalist's verification and onboarding, and their payouts account's onboarding at Stripe ([ADR 0083](0083-payments-are-stripes.md)) |
| Work queue | every notification delivery ([ADR 0084](0084-email-is-postmarks.md), [ADR 0085](0085-sms-is-twilios.md)), the malware scan ([ADR 0086](0086-the-malware-scanner.md)), the payment provider's webhooks, and the purge of a report past its retention |
| Events and audit | the journalist-side access trail of sensitive reports; the pushes that keep a journalist's inbox current |

**The first namespaces**, in the order the loops need them:

| Namespace | Holds | Loop |
|-----------|-------|------|
| `journalists` | the journalist's profile: display name, then bio, coverage areas, topics, links, and the verification badge | all three |
| `community` | follows and a journalist's updates to followers | follow and support |
| `support` | one-time and monthly support, receipts, refunds, and the desk's payouts account | follow and support |
| `reports` | a sent report's deliveries, their journalist-side state (`new`, `reviewing`, `follow-up`, `useful`, `archived`), notes, links to an investigation, and the source follow-up thread | send, and write back |
| `notifications` | the in-app centre, a person's channels and opt-ins, and the deliveries to email and SMS | all three |
| `safety` | verification requests, abuse and threat reports, blocks, rate limits past the gateway's, and retention settings | all three |

`journalists` lands first, with its `Journalist` entity: a `core`-role,
`org`-scoped row that is `Trackable`, since a journalist edits their
profile. It is not `SoftDeletable`: the first release closes no profile
on its own, and a profile goes with its desk, when the org is deleted
and the sweep purges the tenant. Closing a profile while the desk stays
is a delete operation, and the mixin, when a loop needs it. It carries
no version: one journalist edits their own
profile, so a lost update between two tabs of one person is accepted
until a desk has several editors. It has no unique key besides its id,
and its manager owns no field yet; the verification badge is a
manager-owned field when verification lands. The link from a journalist
to the person who writes as them, and the public directory a reader
browses across desks, come with verification: the directory is a read
model the journalists namespace publishes, never a read across orgs.

## Consequences

A reader who supports ten journalists has rows in ten orgs, each fenced
by the desk's `org_id` and readable to the reader only through the
identity scope. A screen that lists "journalists I follow" is an
identity-scoped read and never a join across tenants.

A source cannot be found through the platform: no row, log, or event
names them. What gives way is support: a source who loses their
follow-up secret cannot be recovered, and an operator cannot tell who
sent a report, even under a legal demand.

Anything that needs a report's plaintext (search over its text, a
server-side preview, a scan of its attachments by the platform) happens
on the journalist's client or does not happen. The inbox's server-side
search and filter run over what the platform may see: tags the
journalist sets, the delivery's state, its dates, and the approximate
location when the sender chose to send it in the clear.

A newsroom is a team org with several journalist profiles and its own
members, and needs no change to the tables the first release lands.
# ADR 0087: A visitor acts on a desk from a weaker stage

**Status**: accepted (2026-09-30)

## Context

[ADR 0082](0082-free-journalism-on-the-core.md) puts a follow, a support,
and a report's delivery in the journalist's desk, the org, and says a
reader is never a member of that desk and a source is no identity at all.
The core authorizes a tenant operation through a `TenantContext`, which
only a membership gives. So the three loops of the first release each
need a person who holds no membership in a desk to write one row into it:

- a reader follows a journalist, or opens a checkout to support them;
- a source, with no account, sends a report to one or more journalists,
  and later reads and answers the thread about it.

A new role on the core's ladder, a "visitor" member minted into every
desk a reader touches, would make every reader a user of every desk they
follow, which ADR 0082 refuses, and would widen the role table every
permission test holds.

## Decision

**A reader acts on a desk from the identity stage.** A follow and the
opening of a support are manager operations that take `IdentityContext`
first, the stage the reader's own session proves (`Identity` at the
edge), and the desk's `org_id` beside it. The row names the reader's
`identity_id`, set by the manager from the stage and never taken from the
request, and lands under the desk's `org_id`: the query's predicate and
the table's `tenant_fence` both hold it to that desk. The reader reads
their own rows across desks by identity, a read of the system scope on
the tenantless list, as the core reads a person's memberships
(`read_memberships_by_identity`); never by reading a desk.

**A source acts on a desk from the request stage.** Sending a report,
reading its thread, and answering in it are operations that take
`RequestContext`, since nobody is known. What proves a source's right to
a thread is the follow-up secret their device made: the delivery keeps
its SHA-256 digest, the source presents the secret, and the manager
compares the digests in constant time. A delivery sent with no digest
has no thread a source can reach.

**The desk's own operations stay on the tenant stage.** Listing
followers, supports, and the inbox, opening a delivery, moving its
state, and replying take `TenantContext`, `READ` or `WRITE`, as every
tenant operation does.

**A row a visitor's write lands names no desk user.** The outbox row of
such a write carries the desk's org and `EMPTY_UUID` as its actor
(`visitor_row`), the core's marker for no principal, so the event a
journalist's inbox is pushed carries no one's id, and a source's route
leaves nothing that names them.

**What a visitor sends is idempotent by its own id.** A source holds no
credential, so no idempotency marker can be kept for them. The report and
each message of its thread carry an id the source's device minted, and
the route is a `PUT` of that id: a retry writes nothing new. A follow is
a `PUT` of the reader's follow of one journalist, one per reader and
journalist. A support is a `POST` under the gateway's `Idem`, which the
reader's session carries.

**The report is kept once, in the object store, under the system scope.**
The ciphertext is written to the `sealed-reports` bucket under
`EMPTY_UUID`, the scope no org owns, keyed by the report's id. Each
recipient desk gets a delivery row that names the report and holds its

Every `arch-scaffold-*` skill follows these. A skill's own file says
what it adds: its input, the files it creates and changes, and the
steps that differ.

## The shape is a file

Every file a scaffold writes has a sibling that shows its shape. In a
tree copied from the scaffold, the sibling is the tree's own file at the
path the skill names. When the tree has no such file, it is the
plugin's copy, `../../scaffold/acme_root/<path>` from the skill's
folder, with `acme` read as the tree's name. Read the sibling, its imports, and
its test before writing. Copy its shape, not its domain. A skill states
only what an agent gets wrong from the files alone.

`<name>` is the tree's name, the folder under `om/src/`. Its forms are
snake case for the package, the logins, and the paths (`free_press`),
kebab case for distributions, cloud resources, and domains
(`free-press`), the upper snake prefix for the environment
(`FREE_PRESS_`), and Title case for prose. Never assume `acme` in a
copy.

## Before writing anything

1. Read `version` in `../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, from the
   skill's folder as `realpath` resolves it, and name it in the output
   as "`<version>`, or a later snapshot of main".
2. Read the sections of `architecture.md` the skill names, then the
   sibling files its steps name.
3. Check every path the skill creates. A file that exists, or a folder
   that holds anything, is a collision: stop and say so, and never
   overwrite. An empty folder is no collision; the skill writes into
   it. A migration stamp already used in its role's folder takes the
   next minute.
4. Ask for everything the input lacks in one message, then proceed.
   When no one answers, as in an unattended run, decide each from the
   product's spec or description and the sibling files, name each
   choice in the output after the files, and go on.

## Names

- A namespace `<ns>` (plural, snake case) has a singular: `<Ns>` in
  CamelCase and `<ns_singular>` in snake case (`orders` gives `Order`
  and `order`). Ask when the singular is not a plain one. Its
  interfaces are `<Ns>ManagerInterface` and `<Ns>StorageInterface`, its
  impls `<Ns>ManagerImpl`, `<Ns>StoragePostgresImpl`, and
  `<Ns>StorageMemoryImpl`, and its getters `get_<ns_singular>_storage()`
  and `get_<ns_singular>_service()`. The field on `Managers` is `<ns>`.
- An entity `<Entity>` has `<entity>` and `<entities>` in snake case.
  Manager operations are `get_<entities>`, `get_<entity>`,
  `create_<entity>`, `update_<entity>` (only on a `Trackable` entity),
  and `delete_<entity>` (only on a `SoftDeletable` one). Storage
  operations are `read_<entities>`, `read_<entity>`, `create_<entity>`,
  and `write_<entity>`, and an append-only record has `append_<entity>`
  in place of the last two. Wire types are `<Entity>View`,
  `Add<Entity>Request`, and `Update<Entity>Request` (only beside
  `update_<entity>`).
- A work kind is upper snake case, and its handler is
  `<Kind>HandlerImpl` (`NOTIFY_SHIPMENT` gives
  `NotifyShipmentHandlerImpl`).
- A cloud resource takes the kebab form of the name. The production
  environment is `production` in every name a process, a role, a
  profile, or a resource reads; only its Terraform folders are `prod/`.

## What the files do not say

Each of these holds in every file a scaffold writes, and each is where
a copy of the shape still goes wrong.

- **The context comes first.** A manager or service operation takes its
  stage first: `ctx: TenantContext` for a tenant, `rctx` on the request
  stage for a transition or the sweep, `ictx` for an identity before a
  tenant, and `octx` on the operator plane. A storage method takes
  `org_id: UUID` first. A method that takes no tenant says why in its
  docstring and is listed under `[tool.arch-check.options.CTX-12]
  tenantless` in the root `pyproject.toml` and in
  `om/tests/unit/test_storage_exceptions.py`. A site that builds a
  stage above the request stage is listed under
  `[tool.arch-check.options.CTX-26] sites` and in
  `om/tests/unit/test_stage_construction.py`.
- **A manager stays within its bound.** `arch-check` refuses a manager
  interface of more than twenty operations (CON-01). A project that
  holds another bound sets `max_operations` under
  `[tool.arch-check.options.CON-01]` in the root `pyproject.toml`. In a
  namespace whose manager delegates, a new operation goes to the
  delegate whose duty it is, and to the manager itself only when no
  delegate's duty covers it, as a transition or the sweep.
- **A delegate takes the operations that are added.** When the
  operations a scaffold adds would take a manager past the bound, they
  go to a new delegate, whose duty is theirs, as `tenancy` has
  `credentials`. The operations the manager already holds stay where
  they are. Moving those, with their callers and their tests, is a
  change of its own, made only when a person asks for it.
- **A delegate's shape.** It is `<Ns><Duty>ManagerInterface` in
  `om/src/<name>/om/<ns>/<duty>.py`, re-exported from the package root,
  and `<Ns><Duty>ManagerImpl` in `impl/<duty>.py`. The root builds it in
  `om/src/<name>/om/root.py` and hands it to the manager, whose
  interface carries it as an attribute, never a method. It has no field
  on `Managers`, and a caller outside the namespace reaches it as
  `managers.<ns>.<duty>`. A delegate that calls a sibling takes it in
  its constructor, typed by its interface, as `members` takes `org`. One
  that needs an operation of the manager, a transition among them, takes
  a narrow callable for that one operation, which the root binds at call
  time, as `org` takes `service_context`. The manager holds the
  delegate, so the delegate never takes the manager.
- **Authorize first.** A mutating manager operation opens with
  `ctx.require(<permission>)`, or `octx.require(...)`, before any read,
  the ones a worker calls included. Only an operation on a stage with no
  permissions (the request stage, the identity stage) and the outbox
  handoff open without one.
- **An update copies onto the stored row.** It reads the row, takes the
  caller's fields less `PROVENANCE_FIELDS` and the entity's
  `MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS`, and builds the copy with
  `model_validate({**current.model_dump(), **changes})`, never
  `model_copy(update=...)` over a dump, which skips validation. Every
  entity declares `MANAGER_OWNED_FIELDS`, even when it is empty.
- **The outbox rows ride the write.** A `core`-role write lands its row
  and its `OutboxRow`s in one storage call, and the manager relays them
  at once. A relay that fails is logged and left to the sweep, never
  raised, since the write has committed. Work that follows a write is a
  second row, of kind `work_row_kind(<kind>)`, in the same call, never
  an enqueue the manager makes. A payload, an event, and a socket frame
  carry ids, never a personal field's value.
- **Two fences.** The `org_id` in the query is the fence, and the
  table's row-level security policy is the second. Every table is in
  `TABLE_ROLES` (`om/src/<name>/om/storage/roles.py`) and
  `TABLE_SCOPES` (`storage/scopes.py`), and the migration that creates
  it creates its policy, with `ENABLE` and `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
  Every Postgres statement opens through the base's `_session_for`,
  with the call's scope by keyword. `EMPTY_UUID` is passed only by a
  method on the tenantless list.
- **A backfill lifts the force.** A data migration runs as the
  migration login, which `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` binds, so its
  `UPDATE` would touch nothing. Its SQL lifts the force for the one
  table and puts it back in the same transaction, and raises when the
  rows it touched are not the rows it meant to touch. Its integration
  test seeds two tenants and sees both touched.
- **A cross-tenant case per storage method.** The contract module under
  `om/tests/contracts/` has, for every storage method, a case that
  passes another tenant's id and finds nothing and changes nothing. The
  unit module runs it over memory, the integration module over
  Postgres. Both impls order by the `UUID`, never its string.
- **Two storage impls, one manager impl.** A namespace that fronts an
  outside provider reaches it through a client under `integrations/`,
  with a real impl and a deterministic twin, and the setting that picks
  one.
- **Creates are idempotent.** A route that writes a durable row takes
  the gateway's `Idem` dependency and runs under it, whether it answers
  201 with the row or 202 with the id of work.
- **Every setting is documented and deployed.** A field of a process's
  settings is in `.env.example` under the prefix, and every environment
  under `deployment/terraform/environments/` sets it or wires it as a
  secret. The settings tests hold both.
- **Versions are current.** A library, image, or tool a scaffold adds is
  at its latest stable release that a patch release already follows,
  as Technology Choices and How to Override Them (Versions) states. A
  version the scaffold cannot confirm is named in the output.
- **No placeholder.** No empty module, no `TODO`, no dead import. A
  namespace's `README.md`, and `om/README.md` above it, speak the
  product's language to a reader with no code.

## Changing existing files

A changed file gains an entry: a getter on a root, a field on
`Managers`, a router in `HOSTED`, a row in a map, a member in the
workspace. Nothing is reordered, and nothing is removed but what a
skill's Changed table names as removed.

## After writing

Before the first gate, format what was written with the tree's
formatter, `uv run ruff check --fix .` and then `uv run ruff format .`,
the two the setup target ends with. A formatter run is no gate run,
and no count holds it.

1. Run these, in order, and stop at the first that fails:
   `make infra-up` and `make migrate` when a table was added,
   `make openapi` when a route was added and no step ran it since,
   `make check`, and
   `make migrate-check` when a table was added. The database targets
   run only against the local compose stack, and only when Docker runs
   (`docker info` exits 0). When it does not, they are skipped, and the
   output names each one skipped. A tool runs through the workspace
   (`uv run`, `pnpm run`), never a global install.

   A gate that fails on what the scaffold wrote is fixed, and the
   commands of its step run again from the first: the first run plus at
   most 3 reruns. When the count runs out, stop, and leave the tree as
   the last run left it. A fix edits only files the scaffold created or
   changed.

   Three failures stop at once, with no fix: one that was there before
   the scaffold ran; one of the machine (no network, Docker stopped, a
   port that cannot be moved); and one whose fix takes an exception to
   a rule the guideline states, or removes, skips, or suppresses a
   conformance test. That fix is the person's decision, recorded as an
   ADR.
2. Print the guideline version, then every file created or changed,
   one per line, from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`
   (in a tree with no commit yet, which it lists whole, as the skill
   wrote them), then each command run, once, with the outcome of its
   last run. A stop closes the output with
   `Stopped: <command>: <what went wrong>; <cause>`, the cause one of:
   the count ran out, pre-existing, the machine, needs an exception.

Never commit. A scaffold leaves a working tree for a person to review.
