    # environment's portal callback. A deployed environment names its own
    # and nothing else, over https, never a local address; the local stack
    # names the portal's two local ports. A redirect not named here is
    # refused, so a code is never sent anywhere else.
    sign_in_redirect_uris: list[str] = [
        "http://localhost:55173/auth/callback",
        "http://localhost:5173/auth/callback",
    ]
    # Where the identity provider's logout may send a person back to: this
    # environment's portal page that says they are signed out. Each is also
    # one of the WorkOS application's sign-out URIs. A deployed environment
    # names its own and nothing else, over https; the local stack names the
    # portal's two local ports. A return not named here is refused.
    sign_out_return_uris: list[str] = [
        "http://localhost:55173/signed-out",
        "http://localhost:5173/signed-out",
    ]
    # The sign-in by address alone, with no browser round trip, for the
    # seed, the traffic generator, and the tests. Off unless set, and
    # refused at boot outside a local or test environment.
    dev_sign_in_enabled: bool = False
    # How long an invitation's link works, from its send or resend.
    invitation_lifetime_days: int = Field(default=7, ge=1, le=30)
    # The interactive API docs and the OpenAPI document, served locally for
    # a developer. A deployed environment turns them off: the document is in
    # the repository, and a production edge has no use for a console.
    interactive_docs: bool = True
    # The socket's two send lanes, each bounded on its own. The stream lane
    # holds the event hints, and a full one drops its oldest: the client that
    # sees the gap replays from storage. The control lane holds the frames
    # that say where the socket stands (hello, pong, subscribed,
    # unsubscribed, error), and it is small because a socket offers few of
    # them; a lane that fills is a fault of the process, not a burst.
    realtime_send_buffer_size: int = Field(default=256, gt=0)
    realtime_control_buffer_size: int = Field(default=16, gt=0)
    # How often an open socket asks again whether the credential behind it
    # still holds, in seconds. The bus closes a revoked socket at once; this
    # is the bound when the bus lost the message, and it costs each socket
    # one recheck per interval.
    realtime_recheck_seconds: float = Field(default=300.0, gt=0)
    # How long the tenant's head this process heard on the bus answers a
    # ping without a read, in seconds. It is the longest a hint the bus lost
    # stays hidden from a quiet socket. Zero reads the head on every ping.
    realtime_head_max_age_seconds: float = Field(default=60.0, ge=0)
    # The readiness probe's own deadline, shorter than its prober's timeout
    # (the deploy's check after a rollout gives up at 10 seconds), so a hung
    # database or an exhausted pool makes the probe answer "not ready"
    # instead of making it stop answering. Seconds.
    readiness_timeout_seconds: float = 2.0
    # Admission: the requests this process keeps in flight at once, counted
    # in two budgets, and what a refusal past either tells the client to
    # wait. Reads (GET, HEAD) and writes are budgeted apart so that a read
    # storm, which is what a client that was offline replaying its backlog
    # is, cannot take every slot from the commands. Together they are the one
    # bound the process had, which is a multiple of what it can actually work
    # on: the declared size of the pool it opens per role and no more, since
    # the pools carry no overflow. Reads are the many and writes the few, so
    # that is how the bound is split. A burst still waits briefly on a
    # checkout, which has a bound of its own, and only a flood is refused; it
    # is not the rate limits above, which are fairness between subjects and
    # fail open.
    admission_limit_reads: int = Field(default=400, gt=0)
    admission_limit_writes: int = Field(default=200, gt=0)
    admission_retry_after_seconds: int = 1
    # The deadline of an admitted request, from the moment it takes its slot:
    # every call it makes to a provider or to AWS shares it, and a call still
    # waiting when it passes ends there, so a provider that hangs costs a
    # request this at most instead of its timeouts times its retries (ADR
    # 0069). It sits inside every bound on how long an answer can still reach
    # someone: the portal and the command line give up on a call at 30
    # seconds, a draining task has 45 (15 of deregistration, 30 to stop), and
    # the load balancer 60. The 10 seconds left under the clients' 30 carry
    # the refusal back and the database work around the calls. Seconds.
    request_deadline_seconds: float = Field(default=20.0, gt=0)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def local_doors_stay_local(self) -> ApiSettings:
        """The local sign-in is refused outside a local or test environment,
        and a deployed environment's sign-in and sign-out come back to its own
        https address and nowhere else. Each refusal names the setting."""
        if self.dev_sign_in_enabled and self.environment not in DEV_SIGN_IN_ENVIRONMENTS:
            raise ValueError(
                "FREE_JOURNALISM_DEV_SIGN_IN_ENABLED=true is refused when "
                + f"FREE_JOURNALISM_ENVIRONMENT={self.environment}"
            )
        if self.environment in CLOUD_ENVIRONMENTS:
            for setting, uris, what in (
                ("FREE_JOURNALISM_SIGN_IN_REDIRECT_URIS", self.sign_in_redirect_uris, "sign-in"),
                ("FREE_JOURNALISM_SIGN_OUT_RETURN_URIS", self.sign_out_return_uris, "sign-out"),
            ):
                for uri in uris:
                    parts = urlsplit(uri)
                    if parts.scheme != "https" or parts.hostname in (
                        None,
                        "localhost",
                        "127.0.0.1",
                    ):
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"{setting} names {uri!r}; a deployed environment's "
                            f"{what} comes back to its own https address"
                        )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def the_edge_stands_behind_a_trusted_proxy(self) -> ApiSettings:
        """The edge's hop is counted from the trusted proxies' hops, so an
        edge secret with no trusted proxy has nothing to count from."""
        if self.edge_secret is not None and not self.trusted_proxies:
            raise ValueError("edge_secret is set and trusted_proxies is empty; the edge needs both")
        if self.edge_secret is not None and len(self.edge_secret.get_secret_value()) < 32:
            raise ValueError("edge_secret is shorter than 32 characters")
        return self

from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.om.community import CommunityManagerInterface
from free_journalism.om.community.types.follow import Follow
from free_journalism.om.context import IdentityContext, TenantContext
from free_journalism.services.api.services.community import CommunityServiceInterface
from free_journalism.services.api.services.impl.tenancy import decode_cursor, encode_cursor
from free_journalism.services.api.types.common import clamp_limit
from free_journalism.services.api.types.community import (
    FollowPageView,
    FollowView,
    ReaderFollowPageView,
    ReaderFollowView,
)


def reader_follow_view(org_id: UUID, follow: Follow) -> ReaderFollowView:
    return ReaderFollowView(
        id=follow.id,
        org_id=org_id,
        journalist_id=follow.journalist_id,
        created_at=follow.created_at,
    )


class CommunityServiceImpl(CommunityServiceInterface):
    def __init__(self, community: CommunityManagerInterface) -> None:
        self._community = community

    async def create_follow(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID
    ) -> ReaderFollowView:
        follow = await self._community.create_follow(ictx, org_id, journalist_id)
        return reader_follow_view(org_id, follow)

    async def get_my_follows(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, cursor: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> ReaderFollowPageView:
        after = decode_cursor("my_follows", cursor) if cursor else None
        page = await self._community.get_my_follows(ictx, after, clamp_limit(limit))
        return ReaderFollowPageView(
            items=[reader_follow_view(r.org_id, r.follow) for r in page.items],
            next_cursor=(
                encode_cursor("my_follows", page.items[-1].follow.id) if page.has_more else None
            ),
        )

    async def get_follows(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, cursor: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> FollowPageView:
        after = decode_cursor("follows", cursor) if cursor else None
        page = await self._community.get_follows(ctx, after, clamp_limit(limit))
        return FollowPageView(
            items=[FollowView.model_validate(f) for f in page.items],
            next_cursor=encode_cursor("follows", page.items[-1].id) if page.has_more else None,
        )

"""Community routes: a reader follows a journalist of a desk and lists their
own follows, from their session's identity; the desk lists its followers.
Each function is one call into the community service. A follow is a `PUT`
of the reader's one follow of a journalist, so a retry changes nothing
(ADR 0087)."""

from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import APIRouter

from free_journalism.services.api.gateway.auth import Ctx, Identity
from free_journalism.services.api.gateway.resolve import CommunityService
from free_journalism.services.api.types.common import LIMIT_DEFAULT
from free_journalism.services.api.types.community import (
    FollowPageView,
    ReaderFollowPageView,
    ReaderFollowView,
)

router = APIRouter(tags=["community"])


@router.put("/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist_id}/follow", response_model=ReaderFollowView)
async def create_follow(
    identity: Identity, community: CommunityService, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID
) -> ReaderFollowView:
    """Follow the journalist, for free. Following again answers the follow
    the reader holds."""
    return await community.create_follow(identity, org_id, journalist_id)


@router.get("/follows", response_model=ReaderFollowPageView)
async def list_my_follows(
    identity: Identity,
    community: CommunityService,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = LIMIT_DEFAULT,
) -> ReaderFollowPageView:
    """The signed-in reader's follows across desks, oldest first."""
    return await community.get_my_follows(identity, cursor, limit)


@router.get("/followers", response_model=FollowPageView)
async def list_followers(
    ctx: Ctx, community: CommunityService, cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = LIMIT_DEFAULT
) -> FollowPageView:
    """The desk's followers, oldest first."""
    return await community.get_follows(ctx, cursor, limit)

def build_tenancy(
    storage: TenancyStorageInterface,
    relay: OutboxRelayInterface,
    cache: CacheInterface,
    options: TenancyOptions,
    clock: Callable[[], datetime] = utcnow,
    *,
    identity_provider: IdentityProviderInterface,

    it: a caller outside the namespace reaches a delegate through the
    manager, and no impl builds another. A delegate that calls a sibling
    takes it here, by its interface, and one that needs an operation of the
    manager takes that one operation as a callable. `clock` is the one the
    second factor's time step is read from."""

        storage, relay, options, clock, identity_provider=identity_provider

    # and a stage comes only from the manager's transition. The manager holds
    # this delegate, so that one edge is bound at call time.

        storage,
        relay,
        options,

def interfaces(*suffixes: str) -> list[type]:
    found: list[type] = []
    for module_info in pkgutil.walk_packages(
        free_journalism.om.__path__, prefix="free_journalism.om."
    ):
        module = importlib.import_module(module_info.name)
        for name, obj in vars(module).items():
            if (
                inspect.isclass(obj)
                and name.endswith(suffixes)
                and obj.__module__ == module.__name__
                and name not in suffixes
            ):
                found.append(obj)
    return found


def operations(interface: type) -> list[tuple[str, list[inspect.Parameter]]]:
    result: list[tuple[str, list[inspect.Parameter]]] = []
    for name, member in inspect.getmembers(interface, inspect.iscoroutinefunction):
        if name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        params = list(inspect.signature(member).parameters.values())[1:]
        result.append((name, params))
    return result


def stage_of(param: inspect.Parameter) -> type | None:
    """The stage a first parameter is annotated with, by class or by name (a
    module under `from __future__ import annotations` leaves a string)."""
    annotation = param.annotation
    for stage in STAGES:
        if annotation is stage or annotation == stage.__name__:
            return stage
    return None


def test_storage_methods_take_org_id_first_except_the_documented_ones() -> None:
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for interface in interfaces("StorageInterface"):
        for name, params in operations(interface):
            key = (interface.__name__, name)
            if [p.name for p in params[:1]] == ["org_id"]:
                assert key not in STORAGE_EXCEPTIONS, f"{key} is listed but takes org_id"
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            assert key in STORAGE_EXCEPTIONS, f"{key} does not take org_id first"
            doc = getattr(interface, name).__doc__ or ""
            assert doc.startswith(("Global", "Cross-tenant")), f"{key} lacks its reason"
    assert seen == STORAGE_EXCEPTIONS, f"stale entries: {STORAGE_EXCEPTIONS - seen}"


def test_every_tenant_method_is_named_in_a_cross_tenant_case() -> None:
    """The other half of the rule above. A method that takes `org_id` has a
    contract case presenting another tenant's, so the fence is proven by a
    query that runs and not by a parameter that exists. This reads the names
    the suites declare, so it catches a method that arrives with no case; that
    the named case does what it says is the suites' own business, and what
    happens when a predicate goes is the negative control's."""
    declared = {name for cases in CROSS_TENANT_CASES.values() for name in cases}
    found = {interface.__name__ for interface in interfaces("StorageInterface")}
    assert set(CROSS_TENANT_CASES) == found, "a storage interface with no contract suite named"
    for interface in interfaces("StorageInterface"):
        cases = CROSS_TENANT_CASES[interface.__name__]
        for name, params in operations(interface):
            takes_tenant = [p.name for p in params[:1]] == ["org_id"]
            if takes_tenant:
                assert name in cases, f"({interface.__name__}, {name}) has no cross-tenant case"
            else:
                assert name not in cases, f"({interface.__name__}, {name}) takes no tenant"
        stale = cases - {name for name, _ in operations(interface)}
        assert not stale, f"{interface.__name__} names cases for gone methods: {sorted(stale)}"
    assert declared, "the suites declare no cross-tenant cases at all"

def request_digest(method: str, path: str, body: bytes) -> str:
    """What makes two requests the same request: method, path, and body."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    digest.update(f"{method.upper()}\n{path}\n".encode())
    digest.update(body)
    return digest.hexdigest()

    async def finish(
        self, key: str, attempt_id: UUID, status: int, body: str
    ) -> IdempotencyRecord: ...

    async def release(self, key: str, attempt_id: UUID) -> None: ...

    async def release(self, key: str, attempt_id: UUID) -> None:

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from enum import StrEnum
from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.infra.base import InfraModel
from free_journalism.infra.exceptions import BlobNotFound, InvalidBucketKey, UploadRefused

__all__ = [
    "BlobNotFound",
    "Buckets",
    "BucketsInterface",
    "InvalidBucketKey",
    "PresignedPost",
    "UploadRefused",
    "object_key",
]


class Buckets(StrEnum):
    USER_FILE_UPLOADS = "user-file-uploads"
    EXPORTS = "exports"


def object_key(org_id: UUID, key: str) -> str:
    """The storage key: the tenant first, then the caller's path."""
    if not key or key.startswith("/") or ".." in key.split("/"):
        raise InvalidBucketKey(f"bucket key {key!r} is not a relative path")
    return f"{org_id}/{key}"


class PresignedPost(InfraModel):
    """One bounded upload a browser makes straight to the store: a form POST
    of `fields`, in order, then the file, to `url`. The signed policy in the
    fields carries the content type and a `content-length-range` from zero to
    `max_bytes`; the store refuses a body larger than that, or of another
    type, so a form handed to a browser cannot fill the bucket. A presigned
    PUT cannot bound a body's size, which is why an upload is a POST."""

    url: str
    fields: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]


class BucketsInterface(ABC):
    """A put, get, or exists a request makes carries the request's deadline,
    and ends by then, unreachable (`free_journalism.infra.deadline`); a worker's
    carries none. Presigning makes no call."""

    @abstractmethod
    async def put(
        self,
        org_id: UUID,
        bucket: Buckets,
        key: str,
        data: bytes,
        content_type: str,
        *,
        deadline: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def get(
        self, org_id: UUID, bucket: Buckets, key: str, *, deadline: datetime | None = None
    ) -> bytes: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def exists(
        self, org_id: UUID, bucket: Buckets, key: str, *, deadline: datetime | None = None
    ) -> bool: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def list(
        self, org_id: UUID, bucket: Buckets, prefix: str, limit: int, after: str | None = None
    ) -> list[str]:
        """The tenant's keys under `prefix`, in lexical order, at most `limit`
        of them, strictly after `after` when one is given. The next page
        starts after the last key returned. The caller picks the bound."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def delete(self, org_id: UUID, bucket: Buckets, key: str) -> None: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def presign_get(
        self,
        org_id: UUID,
        bucket: Buckets,
        key: str,
        ttl: timedelta,
        *,
        content_type: str | None = None,
        content_disposition: str | None = None,
    ) -> str | None:
        """A link to one object for `ttl`, or None where the store cannot sign
        (the local impl). `content_type` and `content_disposition`, when
        given, are signed into the link as the headers the store answers
        with: a preview is `inline` under the stored type, a download an
        `attachment` under the file's name."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def presign_post(
        self,
        org_id: UUID,
        bucket: Buckets,
        key: str,
        content_type: str,
        max_bytes: int,
        ttl: timedelta,
    ) -> PresignedPost | None:
        """An upload bounded by `content_type` and `max_bytes`, or None where
        the store cannot presign (the local impl). On None the caller moves
        the bytes through `put` itself and holds them to the same bounds."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def describe(self) -> str: ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def start(self) -> None:
        """Opened by the infra root at boot. An impl that holds no connection
        of its own returns None."""
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Closed by the infra root at shutdown, in reverse order of start."""
        ...

module "queue" {
  source = "../queue"

  environment = var.environment
  prefix      = "free-journalism-${var.environment}-"
  queues      = ["webhooks"] # free_journalism.infra.queues.Queues
}

module "buckets" {
  source = "../buckets"

  environment = var.environment
  prefix      = var.bucket_prefix
  buckets     = ["user-file-uploads", "exports"] # free_journalism.infra.buckets.Buckets
  destroyable = var.destroyable
  # The portal posts a file straight to the uploads bucket with a form the
  # API signed, and fetches it back by a signed link.
  browser_buckets = ["user-file-uploads"]
  browser_origins = concat(["https://${var.app_domain_name}"], var.cors_origins)
  # Every key the media namespace writes is <org_id>/media/<purpose>/<id>.
  object_key_patterns = { "user-file-uploads" = "*/media/*" }
}

module "secrets" {
  source = "../secrets"

  environment               = var.environment
  prefix                    = "free_journalism/${var.environment}/"
  database_password         = ephemeral.random_password.database.result
  database_password_version = var.database_password_version
  database_username         = module.database.username
  database_address          = module.database.address
  database_port             = module.database.port
  database_name             = module.database.db_name

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0137yYm7mttKMGoQWYBVijna","type":"tool_result","content":""""Follows over the live app: a reader follows a journalist of another desk
from their own session and lists their follows across desks; following again
answers the one follow; the desk lists its followers and never sees who; a
journalist the desk does not hold, and a caller with no session, are refused."""

from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from api_support import sign_in_personal


async def a_journalist(client: httpx.AsyncClient, desk: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    added = await client.post(
        "/v1/journalists",
        headers={**desk, "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())},
        json={"display_name": "Ada Reporter"},
    )
    assert added.status_code == 201, added.text
    return added.json()


async def test_a_reader_follows_a_journalist_of_another_desk(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    desk = await sign_in_personal(client, "ada@example.test")
    org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]
    journalist = await a_journalist(client, desk)
    reader = await sign_in_personal(client, "rae@example.test")
    path = f"/v1/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist['id']}/follow"
    followed = await client.put(path, headers=reader)
    assert followed.status_code == 200, followed.text
    follow = followed.json()
    assert (follow["org_id"], follow["journalist_id"]) == (org_id, journalist["id"])
    again = await client.put(path, headers=reader)
    assert again.status_code == 200 and again.json() == follow, "a reader follows once"
    mine = await client.get("/v1/follows", headers=reader)
    assert mine.status_code == 200, mine.text
    assert mine.json() == {"items": [follow], "next_cursor": None}
    followers = await client.get("/v1/followers", headers=desk)
    assert followers.status_code == 200, followers.text
    assert followers.json()["items"] == [
        {
            "id": follow["id"],
            "journalist_id": journalist["id"],
            "created_at": follow["created_at"],
        }
    ], "the desk sees that it is followed, never by whom"
    assert (await client.get("/v1/followers", headers=reader)).json()["items"] == []


async def test_a_readers_follows_are_paged(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    reader = await sign_in_personal(client, "rae@example.test")
    made = []
    for n in range(3):
        desk = await sign_in_personal(client, f"journalist{n}@example.test")
        org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]

    tmp_path: Path,

    integrations: IntegrationsInterface | None = None,
    **overrides: object,
) -> AppContainer:
    """The test container over the memory storage root and the local infra
    root, with the local sign-in on. A test that needs a bound or a deadline
    of its own names the settings it overrides, one that needs storage to
    behave a certain way passes its own root, and one that signs in through
    the identity provider passes the integrations root over the twin. The
    developer's `.env` is never read: its DSN would send every error a test
    raises on purpose to the local tracker."""
    settings = ApiSettings.model_validate(

def boot(settings: ApiSettings) -> None:
    """Settings first, then logging, the process name, the trust store, error
    reporting, and tracing. Every entry point calls it before it builds a
    container; it runs once per process.

    Naming the process is a step of its own, second: every line this boot
    writes carries the service and the environment, and a boot that configures
    no error reporting still names them."""
    global _booted
    if _booted:
        return
    configure_logging(settings.log_level, settings.log_json)
    name_process(settings.service_name, settings.environment)
    install_trust_store()
    configure_error_reporting(
        settings.sentry_dsn, settings.environment, settings.service_name, settings.version
    )
    configure_tracing(
        settings.otel_endpoint,
        settings.service_name,
        timedelta(seconds=settings.otel_timeout_seconds),
    )
    _booted = True

def reader_follow_view(org_id: UUID, follow: Follow) -> ReaderFollowView:
    return ReaderFollowView(
        id=follow.id,
        org_id=org_id,
        journalist_id=follow.journalist_id,
        created_at=follow.created_at,
    )


class CommunityServiceImpl(CommunityServiceInterface):
    def __init__(self, community: CommunityManagerInterface) -> None:
        self._community = community

    async def create_follow(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, journalist_id: UUID
    ) -> ReaderFollowView:
        follow = await self._community.create_follow(ictx, org_id, journalist_id)
        return reader_follow_view(org_id, follow)

    async def get_my_follows(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, cursor: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> ReaderFollowPageView:
        after = decode_cursor("my_follows", cursor) if cursor else None
        page = await self._community.get_my_follows(ictx, after, clamp_limit(limit))
        return ReaderFollowPageView(
            items=[reader_follow_view(r.org_id, r.follow) for r in page.items],
            next_cursor=(
                encode_cursor("my_follows", page.items[-1].follow.id) if page.has_more else None
            ),
        )

    async def get_follows(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, cursor: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> FollowPageView:
        after = decode_cursor("follows", cursor) if cursor else None
        page = await self._community.get_follows(ctx, after, clamp_limit(limit))
        return FollowPageView(
            items=[FollowView.model_validate(f) for f in page.items],
            next_cursor=encode_cursor("follows", page.items[-1].id) if page.has_more else None,
        )

"""One router module per hosted namespace, mounted under /v1 by the app.

`all_routers(namespaces)` answers the routers of the namespaces named, or of
every hosted one when none is named. That is the first form of a split: the
same image, told by `FREE_JOURNALISM_NAMESPACES` which routers to mount, serves one
namespace as a service of its own, and no code changes."""

from collections.abc import Sequence

from fastapi import APIRouter

from free_journalism.services.api.realtime import socket
from free_journalism.services.api.routers import (
    admin,
    community,
    events,
    journalists,
    media,
    tenancy,
)

HOSTED: dict[str, tuple[APIRouter, ...]] = {
    # The operator plane is tenancy's: it lists and deletes orgs.
    "tenancy": (tenancy.router, admin.router),
    # The realtime channel is the events stream pushed; its replay is `/events`.
    "events": (events.router, socket.router),
    "media": (media.router,),
    "journalists": (journalists.router, journalists.desks_router),
    "community": (community.router,),
}
"""Every namespace this image hosts, and the routers that serve it."""


def all_routers(namespaces: Sequence[str] = ()) -> list[APIRouter]:
    """The routers to mount; a name this image does not host refuses the boot."""
    unknown = sorted(set(namespaces) - set(HOSTED))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"FREE_JOURNALISM_NAMESPACES names {', '.join(unknown)}; this image hosts {', '.join(HOSTED)}"
        )
    chosen = namespaces or tuple(HOSTED)
    return [router for name in HOSTED if name in chosen for router in HOSTED[name]]

        for name, obj in vars(module).items():

def operations(interface: type) -> list[tuple[str, list[inspect.Parameter]]]:
    result: list[tuple[str, list[inspect.Parameter]]] = []
    for name, member in inspect.getmembers(interface, inspect.iscoroutinefunction):
        if name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        params = list(inspect.signature(member).parameters.values())[1:]
        result.append((name, params))
    return result

any purpose accepts, and not a byte more. A route that moves a file's bytes
through the API (for a store that cannot presign) binds it; the manager then
holds the bytes to the file's own size."""

MAX_BODY_BYTES = max(bounds.max_bytes for bounds in BOUNDS.values())


async def bounded_body(request: Request) -> bytes:
    """The body, refused as soon as it passes the bound: a declared length
    past it before a byte is read, and a stream that runs past it as it runs.
    A length is ASCII digits alone: `isdigit` admits the digits of every
    script, some of which `int` refuses, and one written otherwise declares
    nothing. One with more digits than `int` reads is past the bound."""
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared is not None and declared.isascii() and declared.isdigit():
        try:
            past = int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES
        except ValueError:
            past = True
        if past:
            raise ValidationFailed(f"a body is at most {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes")
    chunks: list[bytes] = []
    read = 0
    async for chunk in request.stream():
        read += len(chunk)
        if read > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise ValidationFailed(f"a body is at most {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes")
        chunks.append(chunk)
    return b"".join(chunks)

class RateLimited(PlatformException):

    visitor: RateLimit

    writes: RateLimit
    failed_authentications: RateLimit

class RefusedAddresses:
    """The addresses whose failed authentications spent the shared budget,
    each until the end of the window the shared count named. The shared
    count decides; this process only remembers the answer it was given, so
    a refusal costs no round trip at all. Another replica learns it from its
    own next failure from that address. An entry is added only past a spent
    budget and dropped when its window ends."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._until: dict[str, float] = {}

    def refused_for(self, address: str) -> timedelta | None:
        until = self._until.get(address)
        if until is None:
            return None
        left = until - time.monotonic()
        if left <= 0:
            del self._until[address]
            return None
        return timedelta(seconds=left)

    def refuse(self, address: str, left: timedelta) -> None:
        now = time.monotonic()
        self._until = {a: u for a, u in self._until.items() if u > now}
        self._until[address] = now + left.total_seconds()

# Journalists

The journalists a desk holds, and the profile readers know each one by.
This is one of the kinds of thing
[Free Journalism is made of](../../../../README.md).

## What it holds

- **Journalist**: one journalist's profile at their desk: the display
  name readers see, who made the profile and when, and who changed it
  last. A desk is an org, and an org may hold more than one journalist,
  so a newsroom is a desk with several.

What a profile will also hold, as the product grows: a bio, the places
and topics the journalist covers, their published links and current
investigations, and the badge the platform gives a journalist it has
verified.

## What can happen

- **Add a journalist** to the desk. A member of the desk makes the
  profile, with its display name. Sending the same request twice makes
  one profile.
- **List** the desk's journalists, oldest first, a page at a time.
- **Read** one journalist's profile.
- **Change** a profile's display name. Who made the profile, and when,
  never change.
- **Sweep.** When a desk is deleted, its journalists go with it once the
  desk's retention has passed.

## The rules

- **A profile is its desk's.** A journalist of another desk is answered
  as one that never existed.
- **Viewers read; members write.** A viewer of the desk reads its
  journalists; a member, an admin, or the owner adds and changes them.
- **Changes carry ids.** What the platform announces about a change to
  a profile names the profile's id, never its name.

# Files

The files an org keeps, as references to objects in the store. This is
one of the kinds of thing [Free Journalism is made of](../../../../README.md).

## What it holds

- **File**: a record of one object in the store, never the bytes: the
  name it had on the uploader's computer, its extension, its type, its
  size, who uploaded it, its purpose, and the subject it belongs to,
  when its purpose has one. The bytes live under the org's own prefix
  in the store.
- **Purpose**: why the file is there, which decides its bounds and what
  its subject names. The core has one, `upload`: a file a member keeps
  in the org, with no subject, of at most 100 MB, an image, a document,
  a sound, or a video.
- **Status**: `pending` while the upload is under way, `stored` once
  the object is in the store.
- **Storage used**: the org's files counted per purpose, stored and
  pending.

- **Start an upload** (`POST /v1/media/files`). A pending record is
  made. No bytes move yet.
- **Upload.** The uploader gets a form their browser posts straight to
  the store, good for a few minutes and for this one file. A store that
  cannot sign a form takes the bytes through the API instead.
- **Confirm.** Free Journalism looks for the object; only then is the file stored.

def configure_logging(level: str, json_logs: bool) -> None:
    root = logging.getLogger()
    for handler in list(root.handlers):
        root.removeHandler(handler)
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
    handler.addFilter(RequestIdFilter())
    if json_logs:
        handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
    else:
        handler.setFormatter(
            logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)-5s [%(request_id)s] %(name)s: %(message)s")
        )
    root.addHandler(handler)
    root.setLevel(level.upper())

"""What the scrubber blanks wherever it appears in an event, headers and

ERROR_REPORTING_PRIVACY: dict[str, Any] = {

    "send_default_pii": False,

def outgoing_event(event: Any, hint: Any) -> Any:
    """The last word on an event before it leaves. It takes the request id as
    a tag. Of the request it keeps the method alone: the SDK's web
    integration fills `request` with the URL, the query string, and the
    headers, each the caller's own text, and the tracker shows an event to
    whoever looks into the request. The route is the event's transaction; a
    request no route took is named by its URL there, so it is `unmatched`."""
    request_id = request_id_var.get()
    if request_id:
        event.setdefault("tags", {})["request_id"] = request_id
    request = event.get("request")
    if isinstance(request, dict):
        event["request"] = {key: request[key] for key in ("method",) if key in request}
    info = event.get("transaction_info")
    if isinstance(info, dict) and info.get("source") == "url":
        event["transaction"] = "unmatched"
    return event


def configure_error_reporting(
    dsn: str | None, environment: str, service_name: str, release: str | None = None
) -> None:
    """Sentry-compatible reporting (GlitchTip locally), only when a DSN is set.
    Unhandled exceptions and ERROR log records become events, tagged with the
    service and the request id; traces stay with OpenTelemetry."""
    if not dsn:
        return

    sentry_sdk.init(
        dsn=dsn,
        environment=environment,
        release=f"{service_name}@{release}" if release else None,
        server_name=service_name,
        traces_sample_rate=0.0,
        before_send=outgoing_event,
        **ERROR_REPORTING_PRIVACY,
    )
    sentry_sdk.set_tag("service", service_name)


def failure_level(error: BaseException) -> int:
    """The level a boundary logs a failure at. The unavailable shape says "not
    right now": a dependency did not answer in time, and the caller comes
    back. That is a warning, which the tracker does not take for an event;
    the counters are what watch it. Any other failure is an error, which the
    tracker reports. The shape is read by its code, which both exception
    roots carry, never by its class."""
    if getattr(error, "code", None) == InfraUnavailable.code:
        return logging.WARNING
    return logging.ERROR

    """The one client that sends traces out; every export is bounded by the
    timeout from settings."""
    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    processor = SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter)
    provider.add_span_processor(processor)
    try:

def held(span: ReadableSpan) -> str:
    """What a reader of the trace is shown of a span: its name, the value of
    each attribute, and whatever its events carry."""
    values = [span.name, *(str(v) for v in (span.attributes or {}).values())]
    for event in span.events:
        values += [event.name, *(str(v) for v in (event.attributes or {}).values())]
    return " ".join([*values, span.status.description or ""])

    named by the route, or `unmatched`, and no attribute holds the rest."""

class SupportStorageInterface(ABC):

    async def read_supports(self, org_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> list[Support]:

    async def read_supports_by_identity(

        after `after`, at most `limit`, each with its desk. Takes no tenant: a
        reader's list spans the desks they support, so it reads in the system
        scope, as the core reads a person's memberships, and the identity is

        ...

    async def create_support(

        `PreconditionFailed` otherwise, landing nothing. Another tenant's row
        is no row here."""
        ...

    async def purge_tenant(self, org_id: UUID, limit: int) -> int:
        """At most `limit` supports of a deleted tenant past its retention;
        returns how many."""
        ...

from typing import ClassVar
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

LIMIT_DEFAULT = 50
LIMIT_MAX = 200


class View(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, from_attributes=True)

    secret_fields: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset()
    """The fields that carry a secret in the clear, shown once: the gateway
    stores the idempotent outcome with each of them absent, so a replay answers
    with the row and no secret. Every such field is optional on the wire."""


class RequestBody(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class StreamTruncatedDetail(View):
    """What a `stream_truncated` refusal carries: the floor, the highest seq
    trimmed from the stream, and the head. A client drops its cursor, reads
    afresh what it shows, and goes on from the head."""

    floor: int
    head: int


class OwnedOrgRef(View):
    """An org named in a refusal: enough to find it and to say which."""

    id: UUID
    name: str
    slug: str


class LastOwnerDetail(View):
    """What a `last_owner` refusal carries: every team org the person is the
    last owner of, which they hand on or delete before their account goes."""

    orgs: list[OwnedOrgRef]


class ErrorBody(View):
    code: str
    message: str
    request_id: UUID
    stream: StreamTruncatedDetail | None = None
    last_owner: LastOwnerDetail | None = None


class ErrorResponse(View):
    error: ErrorBody


def clamp_limit(limit: int) -> int:
    """Lists return a bare list with a server-clamped limit."""
    return max(1, min(limit, LIMIT_MAX))

field names match one-to-one. JSON columns take the JSON-mode dump; scalars
travel natively; enums travel as their value."""

from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy import inspect
from sqlalchemy.sql import sqltypes


def to_row[R](entity: BaseModel, row_type: type[R], **extra: Any) -> R:
    """Build a row from an entity; `extra` carries storage-only columns such as org_id."""
    row = row_type()
    apply_row(row, entity)
    for name, value in extra.items():
        setattr(row, name, value)
    return row


def to_model[M: BaseModel](row: Any, model_type: type[M]) -> M:
    return model_type.model_validate(row, from_attributes=True)


def apply_row(row: Any, entity: BaseModel) -> None:
    """Copy entity values onto an existing row in place, never touching org_id."""
    for name, value in to_values(entity, type(row)).items():
        setattr(row, name, value)


def to_values(entity: BaseModel, row_type: type[Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The column values of an entity, for a statement that writes columns by
    name; org_id and columns the entity has no field for are left out."""
    columns = inspect(row_type).columns
    dumped: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    values: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for name in type(entity).model_fields:
        if name == "org_id" or name not in columns:
            continue
        value = getattr(entity, name)
        if isinstance(columns[name].type, sqltypes.JSON):
            if dumped is None:
                dumped = entity.model_dump(mode="json")
            value = dumped[name]
        elif isinstance(value, Enum):
            value = value.value
        values[name] = value
    return values


def undeletes(stored: Any, entity: Any) -> bool:
    """True when writing `entity` over `stored` would clear a soft delete.
    Takes a table row or an entity on either side: both spell the field
    `deleted_at`, and a type without one is never soft-deleted."""
    return (
        getattr(stored, "deleted_at", None) is not None
        and getattr(entity, "deleted_at", None) is None
    )

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KrNf3mePhvfF8oSLSEtwtB","type":"tool_result","content":""""Follows over the live app: a reader follows a journalist of another desk
from their own session and lists their follows across desks; following again
answers the one follow; the desk lists its followers and never sees who; a
journalist the desk does not hold, and a caller with no session, are refused."""

from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from api_support import sign_in_personal


async def a_journalist(client: httpx.AsyncClient, desk: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    added = await client.post(
        "/v1/journalists",
        headers={**desk, "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())},
        json={"display_name": "Ada Reporter"},
    )
    assert added.status_code == 201, added.text
    return added.json()


async def test_a_reader_follows_a_journalist_of_another_desk(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    desk = await sign_in_personal(client, "ada@example.test")
    org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]
    journalist = await a_journalist(client, desk)
    reader = await sign_in_personal(client, "rae@example.test")
    path = f"/v1/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist['id']}/follow"
    followed = await client.put(path, headers=reader)
    assert followed.status_code == 200, followed.text
    follow = followed.json()
    assert (follow["org_id"], follow["journalist_id"]) == (org_id, journalist["id"])
    again = await client.put(path, headers=reader)
    assert again.status_code == 200 and again.json() == follow, "a reader follows once"
    mine = await client.get("/v1/follows", headers=reader)
    assert mine.status_code == 200, mine.text
    assert mine.json() == {"items": [follow], "next_cursor": None}
    followers = await client.get("/v1/followers", headers=desk)
    assert followers.status_code == 200, followers.text
    assert followers.json()["items"] == [
        {
            "id": follow["id"],
            "journalist_id": journalist["id"],
            "created_at": follow["created_at"],
        }
    ], "the desk sees that it is followed, never by whom"
    assert (await client.get("/v1/followers", headers=reader)).json()["items"] == []


async def test_a_readers_follows_are_paged(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    reader = await sign_in_personal(client, "rae@example.test")
    made = []
    for n in range(3):
        desk = await sign_in_personal(client, f"journalist{n}@example.test")
        org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]
        journalist = await a_journalist(client, desk)
        path = f"/v1/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist['id']}/follow"
        made.append((await client.put(path, headers=reader)).json()["id"])
    first = (await client.get("/v1/follows", headers=reader, params={"limit": 2})).json()
    assert [f["id"] for f in first["items"]] == made[:2] and first["next_cursor"]
    rest = await client.get(
        "/v1/follows", headers=reader, params={"limit": 2, "cursor": first["next_cursor"]}
    )
    assert [f["id"] for f in rest.json()["items"]] == made[2:]


async def test_a_journalist_the_desk_does_not_hold_is_not_found(
    client: httpx.AsyncClient,
) -> None:
    desk = await sign_in_personal(client, "ada@example.test")
    journalist = await a_journalist(client, desk)
    other = await sign_in_personal(client, "bea@example.test")
    other_org = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=other)).json()["id"]
    reader = await sign_in_personal(client, "rae@example.test")
    refused = await client.put(
        f"/v1/desks/{other_org}/journalists/{journalist['id']}/follow", headers=reader
    )
    assert refused.status_code == 404, refused.text
    assert (await client.get("/v1/follows", headers=reader)).json()["items"] == []


async def test_a_follow_needs_a_session(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    desk = await sign_in_personal(client, "ada@example.test")
    org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]
    journalist = await a_journalist(client, desk)
    path = f"/v1/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist['id']}/follow"
    assert (await client.put(path)).status_code == 401
    assert (await client.get("/v1/follows")).status_code == 401
    assert (await client.get("/v1/followers")).status_code == 401


async def test_a_public_profile_needs_no_session(client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
    desk = await sign_in_personal(client, "ada@example.test")
    org_id = (await client.get("/v1/orgs/current", headers=desk)).json()["id"]
    key = "A" * 43 + "="
    added = await client.post(
        "/v1/journalists",
        headers={**desk, "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())},
        json={"display_name": "Ada Reporter", "public_key": key},
    )
    assert added.status_code == 201, added.text
    journalist = added.json()
    public = await client.get(f"/v1/desks/{org_id}/journalists/{journalist['id']}")
    assert public.status_code == 200, public.text
    assert public.json() == {
        "id": journalist["id"],
        "org_id": org_id,
        "display_name": "Ada Reporter",
        "public_key": key,
    }
    missing = await client.get(f"/v1/desks/{uuid4()}/journalists/{journalist['id']}")
    assert missing.status_code == 404
    bad = await client.patch(
        f"/v1/journalists/{journalist['id']}", headers=desk, json={"public_key": "!" * 44}
    )
    assert bad.status_code == 422, bad.text

    def __init__(self, journalists: JournalistsManagerInterface) -> None:
        self._journalists = journalists

    async def create_journalist(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, body: AddJournalistRequest, journalist_id: UUID
    ) -> JournalistView:
        now = utcnow()
        journalist = Journalist(
            id=journalist_id,
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
            created_by=ctx.user_id,
            updated_by=ctx.user_id,
            display_name=body.display_name,
            public_key=body.public_key,

    async def get_journalists(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, cursor: str | None, limit: int
    ) -> JournalistPageView:
        after = decode_cursor("journalists", cursor) if cursor else None
        page = await self._journalists.get_journalists(ctx, after, clamp_limit(limit))
        return JournalistPageView(
            items=[journalist_view(j) for j in page.items],
            next_cursor=encode_cursor("journalists", page.items[-1].id) if page.has_more else None,
        )

    async def get_journalist(self, ctx: TenantContext, journalist_id: UUID) -> JournalistView:
        return journalist_view(await self._journalists.get_journalist(ctx, journalist_id))

    async def update_journalist(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, journalist_id: UUID, body: UpdateJournalistRequest
    ) -> JournalistView:
        current = await self._journalists.get_journalist(ctx, journalist_id)
        changed = Journalist.model_validate(
            {**current.model_dump(), **body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)}
        )
        return journalist_view(await self._journalists.update_journalist(ctx, changed))

    ) -> PublicJournalistView:

        return PublicJournalistView(
            id=journalist.id,
            org_id=org_id,
            display_name=journalist.display_name,
            public_key=journalist.public_key,
        )

    """A journalist as anyone may see them, with no account: the desk, the

from sqlalchemy import Update, select, update

from free_journalism.om.base import EMPTY_UUID
from free_journalism.om.exceptions import PreconditionFailed, TenantMismatch
from free_journalism.om.outbox.storage.tables.outbox_rows import OutboxRows
from free_journalism.om.outbox.types.row import OutboxRow
from free_journalism.om.storage.impl.pg_base import PgStorageBase, delete_batch, deleted
from free_journalism.om.storage.utils.translation import to_model, to_row, to_values
from free_journalism.om.support.storage import SupportStorageInterface
from free_journalism.om.support.storage.tables.supports import Supports
from free_journalism.om.support.types.page import ReaderSupport
from free_journalism.om.support.types.support import Support


def cas_statement(org_id: UUID, support: Support, expected_version: int) -> Update:
    """The compare-and-set of one support: the version is in the WHERE, so two
    writers from one snapshot cannot both land. Returns the id when it hit."""
    values = {k: v for k, v in to_values(support, Supports).items() if k != "id"}
    return (
        update(Supports)
        .where(
            Supports.id == support.id,
            Supports.org_id == org_id,
            Supports.version == expected_version,
        )
        .values(**values)
        .returning(Supports.id)
    )


class SupportStoragePostgresImpl(PgStorageBase, SupportStorageInterface):
    async def read_support(self, org_id: UUID, support_id: UUID) -> Support | None:
        stmt = select(Supports).where(Supports.org_id == org_id, Supports.id == support_id)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            row = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
            return None if row is None else to_model(row, Support)

    async def read_supports(self, org_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> list[Support]:
        stmt = select(Supports).where(Supports.org_id == org_id)
        if after is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(Supports.id > after)
        stmt = stmt.order_by(Supports.id).limit(limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            return [to_model(row, Support) for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars()]

    async def read_supports_by_identity(
        self, identity_id: UUID, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> list[ReaderSupport]:
        stmt = select(Supports).where(Supports.identity_id == identity_id)
        if after is not None:
            stmt = stmt.where(Supports.id > after)
        stmt = stmt.order_by(Supports.id).limit(limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=EMPTY_UUID) as session:
            return [
                ReaderSupport(org_id=row.org_id, support=to_model(row, Support))
                for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars()
            ]

    async def create_support(
        self, org_id: UUID, support: Support, outbox_rows: tuple[OutboxRow, ...]
    ) -> bool:
        if await self._insert(Supports, org_id, support, outbox_rows):
            return True
        # The id is taken: a retry under this tenant, or another tenant's row,
        # which the policy hides from this read.
        if await self.read_support(org_id, support.id) is None:
            raise TenantMismatch(f"support {support.id} is not in {org_id}")
        return False

    async def write_support(
        self,
        org_id: UUID,
        support: Support,
        expected_version: int,
        outbox_rows: tuple[OutboxRow, ...],
    ) -> None:
        async with self._session_for(Supports, org_id=org_id) as session:
            stmt = cas_statement(org_id, support, expected_version)
            if (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none() is None:
                # Moved by another writer, or gone: either way the caller's
                # snapshot is stale. Only a row read under this tenant is
                # ever written, so the question of whose row it is never arises.
                await session.rollback()
                raise PreconditionFailed(
                    f"support {support.id} is no longer at version {expected_version}"
                )
            for outbox_row in outbox_rows:
                session.add(to_row(outbox_row, OutboxRows, org_id=org_id))
            await session.commit()

    async def purge_tenant(self, org_id: UUID, limit: int) -> int:
        stmt = delete_batch(Supports, Supports.org_id == org_id, limit=limit)
        async with self._session_for(stmt, org_id=org_id) as session:
            purged = deleted(await session.execute(stmt))
            await session.commit()
            return purged

def build_loop(container: WorkerContainer, lane: str | None = None) -> WorkerLoop:
    managers = container.managers
    return WorkerLoop(
        work=managers.work,
        outbox=managers.outbox,
        # Per tenant, what only a tenant deleted past its retention has: every
        # row of it goes. Any other tenant costs these nothing.
        purges={
            # Every file's object, then its row.
            "media": managers.media.purge_tenant,
            "tenancy": managers.tenancy.purge_tenant,
            "events": managers.events.purge_tenant,
            "orchestrations": managers.orchestrations.purge_tenant,
            "journalists": managers.journalists.purge_tenant,
            "community": managers.community.purge_tenant,
        },
        # Once a pass, across every tenant: each namespace's rows past their
        # retention.
        across={
            # A deleted file's object, then its row; an abandoned upload's too.
            "media": unstaged(managers.media.purge_across_tenants),
            "tenancy": unstaged(managers.tenancy.purge_across_tenants),
            "idempotency": unstaged(managers.idempotency.purge_across_tenants),
            # The trim: each tenant's floor moves with its events.
            "events": unstaged(managers.events.purge_across_tenants),
            "orchestrations": unstaged(managers.orchestrations.purge_across_tenants),
        },
        # The media purge's batch is its own: a whole one says there may be more.
            retention=timedelta(days=settings.tenancy_retention_days),
            ticket_retention=timedelta(hours=settings.socket_ticket_retention_hours),
            sign_in_delay_retention=timedelta(hours=settings.sign_in_delay_retention_hours),
            purge_batch=batch,
        ),
        integrations=integrations,
        media_options=MediaOptions(
            retention=timedelta(days=settings.media_retention_days),
            pending_expiry=timedelta(hours=settings.media_pending_expiry_hours),
            purge_batch=MEDIA_PURGE_BATCH,
        ),
        idempotency_options=IdempotencyOptions(
            retention=timedelta(hours=settings.idempotency_retention_hours), purge_batch=batch
        ),
        events_options=events_options(settings),
        work_options=WorkOptions(
            retention=timedelta(days=settings.work_retention_days), purge_batch=batch
        ),
        orchestrations_options=OrchestrationsOptions(purge_batch=batch),
        journalists_options=JournalistsOptions(purge_batch=batch),
        community_options=CommunityOptions(purge_batch=batch),
    )

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Unh97P3h7s8K4qLrmsgoM9","type":"tool_result","content":"# What Free Journalism is made of

This page names the things Free Journalism is made of and says how they relate.
It is written for anyone; you need no code to read it. Each kind of
thing has a page of its own one level down, which says what can happen
to it and which rules always hold. A product built on Free Journalism adds its own
kinds beside these.

## The org and the people in it

An **organization**, org for short, is one tenant: a company, a team, a
household. Everything in Free Journalism belongs to exactly one org, and nothing
in one org can see anything in another. That is a rule, not a choice.

Every person has one **personal org**, made with them the first time
they sign in. It is theirs for as long as they exist, and it goes only
with their account. Every other org is a **team org**, which a person
makes and owns.

An **identity** is one person across every org: the email the sign-in
provider has verified. Free Journalism keeps no password.

A **user** is that person inside one org: the name the org sees.

A **membership** is the user's place in the org, with a role: viewer,
member, admin, or owner. The role decides what the person may do there.

An **invitation** asks a person to join an org, by email, with a role.
The sign-in provider sends the email.

## How a person proves who they are

A **session** is a signed-in visit to one org. It ends when the person
signs out, when it sits idle too long, or when it reaches its lifetime.

An **API key** is a named, expiring credential for a program, with a
role no higher than its maker's. Free Journalism keeps only its fingerprint, so
the key is shown once.

A **socket ticket** is a one-use pass that opens the live channel, the
connection through which changes reach a screen as they happen.

An **operator** is a person on the platform's own allowlist. An
operator works across orgs with an **operator token**: one permission,
an hour at most.

## Journalists

A **journalist** is a profile at a desk: the name readers know the
journalist by. A **desk** is the org a journalist works in, at first the
journalist's personal org; a newsroom is a desk with several
journalists. Readers are not people of the desk: what they do about a
journalist (follow, support, send information) belongs to the desk and
names them, and each of those is free of the others.

## Files

A **file** is a record of something an org keeps in the object store:
its name, type, size, who uploaded it, and why. The bytes live in the
store, never in the record.

## What the platform writes for itself

No person creates these and no screen shows them, but each belongs to
an org like everything else.

An **event** is a line in the org's diary: what changed, how, by whom,
and when. The lines are numbered with no gaps. An **audit entry** is an
event the platform records about itself, such as a job that failed for
good.

An **outbox row** is a note written in the same stroke as a change,
saying "tell everyone about this". The event and the live push come
from it, so no change goes unannounced.

A **work item** is a job for later. It waits in a queue until a worker
claims it, holds it for a short lease, and does it.

An **orchestration** is a long job kept as a record, done one step at a
time. It succeeds, fails, or parks until what it waits for is back.

An **idempotency record** remembers the outcome of a request that may
arrive twice, so the second copy gets the first one's answer.

## How they fit together

- An org has users. A user is one identity's place in the org, held by
  a membership with a role.
- A desk has journalists. A journalist belongs to exactly one desk, and
  another desk's journalist is one that does not exist.
- A session or an API key belongs to a user, so everything done with
  it is done as that user in that org.
- Every change a screen acts on writes an outbox row, which becomes an
  event in the org's diary, which reaches every open screen of the org.
- A work item, an orchestration, an idempotency record, an event, and
  an outbox row each name their org, so the fence between orgs holds
  for them too.

from uuid import UUID

from free_journalism.integrations.exceptions import ProviderRefused, ProviderUnavailable

class SupportOptions(Platform):
    max_limit: int = 200
    purge_batch: int = 1000  # supports one purge statement deletes at most
    platform_fee_basis_points: int = 500  # the platform's fee, 5% (ADR 0083)
    checkout_return_url: str
    """The page the provider sends the reader back to, with the support's id
    and the outcome in its query. Empty in a process that opens no
    checkout."""


class SupportManagerImpl(SupportManagerInterface):
    def __init__(
        self,
        storage: SupportStorageInterface,
        journalists: JournalistsManagerInterface,
        tenancy: TenancyManagerInterface,
        relay: OutboxRelayInterface,
        payments: PaymentsProviderInterface,
        options: SupportOptions,
    ) -> None:
        self._storage = storage
        self._journalists = journalists
        self._tenancy = tenancy
        self._relay = relay
        self._payments = payments
        self._options = options

    async def create_support(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, support: Support
    ) -> Support:
        # The identity stage holds no permission of the desk: what bounds the
        # write is that it names the stage's own identity, in the desk named.
        await self._journalists.get_public_journalist(ictx, org_id, support.journalist_id)
        now = utcnow()
        fresh = Support.model_validate(
            {
                **support.model_dump(),
                "created_at": now,
                "updated_at": now,
                # A visitor is no user of the desk (ADR 0087).
                "created_by": EMPTY_UUID,
                "updated_by": EMPTY_UUID,
                "version": 1,
                "identity_id": ictx.identity_id,
                "status": SupportStatus.PENDING,
                "checkout_id": None,
                "checkout_url": None,
            }
        )
        rows = (visitor_row(ictx, org_id, "support.support.created", fresh.id, {"version": 1}),)
        if await self._storage.create_support(org_id, fresh, rows):
            await self._relay.relay_all(org_id, rows)
            held = fresh
        else:
            # A retry under the same id: the row it made is the answer, if it
            # is this reader's.
            stored = await self._storage.read_support(org_id, fresh.id)
            if stored is None:
                raise TenantMismatch(f"support {fresh.id} is not in {org_id}")
            if stored.identity_id != ictx.identity_id:
                raise NotFound(f"support {fresh.id} not found")
            held = stored
        if held.status is not SupportStatus.PENDING:
            return held
        return await self._open(ictx, org_id, held)

    async def _open(self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, pending: Support) -> Support:
        """Opens the provider's checkout for a pending support and writes it
        open. A provider that fails leaves the row pending for a retry."""
        checkout = await self._checkout(ictx, org_id, pending)
        moved = opened(pending, checkout.id, checkout.url, utcnow(), EMPTY_UUID)
        rows = (
            visitor_row(
                ictx, org_id, "support.support.updated", moved.id, {"version": moved.version}
            ),
        )
        try:
            await self._storage.write_support(org_id, moved, pending.version, rows)
        except PreconditionFailed:
            # Two retries at once: the other one's checkout is the answer, and
            # this one's lapses unpaid at the provider.
            stored = await self._storage.read_support(org_id, pending.id)
            if stored is None or stored.checkout_url is None:
                raise
            return stored
        await self._relay.relay_all(org_id, rows)
        return moved

    async def _checkout(self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, support: Support) -> Checkout:
        base = self._options.checkout_return_url
        if not base:
            raise Unavailable("this process opens no checkout")

        def back(outcome: str) -> str:
            return f"{base}?{urlencode({'support': str(support.id), 'outcome': outcome})}"

        request = CheckoutRequest(
            reference=support.id,
            org_id=org_id,
            amount=support.amount,
            currency=support.currency,
            cadence=Cadence(support.cadence.value),
            application_fee=application_fee(
                support.amount, self._options.platform_fee_basis_points
            ),
            success_url=back("success"),
            cancel_url=back("cancel"),
        )
        try:
            return await self._payments.open_checkout(request, deadline=ictx.deadline)
        except ProviderRefused as error:
            raise ValidationFailed(f"the checkout was not opened: {error.message}") from None
        except ProviderUnavailable as error:
            raise Unavailable(f"support is not available: {error.message}") from None

    async def get_my_support(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, org_id: UUID, support_id: UUID
    ) -> Support:
        support = await self._storage.read_support(org_id, support_id)
        if support is None or support.identity_id != ictx.identity_id:
            raise NotFound(f"support {support_id} not found")
        return support

    async def get_my_supports(
        self, ictx: IdentityContext, after: UUID | None, limit: int
    ) -> ReaderSupportPage:
        limit = max(1, min(limit, self._options.max_limit))
        rows = await self._storage.read_supports_by_identity(ictx.identity_id, after, limit + 1)
        return ReaderSupportPage(items=tuple(rows[:limit]), has_more=len(rows) > limit)

    async def get_supports(self, ctx: TenantContext, after: UUID | None, limit: int) -> SupportPage:
        ctx.require(Permission.READ)
        limit = max(1, min(limit, self._options.max_limit))
        rows = await self._storage.read_supports(ctx.org_id, after, limit + 1)
        return SupportPage(items=tuple(rows[:limit]), has_more=len(rows) > limit)

    async def record_payment(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, support_id: UUID, checkout_id: str, status: SupportStatus
    ) -> bool:
        ctx.require(Permission.WRITE)
        if status not in OUTCOMES:
            raise ValidationFailed(f"a payment does not record {status.value}")
        current = await self._storage.read_support(ctx.org_id, support_id)
        if current is None:
            raise NotFound(f"support {support_id} not found")
        if current.checkout_id != checkout_id or not can_move(current.status, status):
            # Another checkout's delivery, a copy of one applied, or a support
            # that moves no more: nothing changes.
            return False
        moved = recorded(current, status, utcnow(), ctx.user_id)
        rows = (versioned_row(ctx, "support.support.updated", moved.id, moved.version),)
        try:
            await self._storage.write_support(ctx.org_id, moved, current.version, rows)
        except PreconditionFailed:
            # Two copies at once: the other one moved it first.
            stored = await self._storage.read_support(ctx.org_id, support_id)
            if stored is not None and not can_move(stored.status, status):
                return False
            raise
        await self._relay.relay_all(ctx.org_id, rows)
        return True

    async def purge_tenant(self, ctx: TenantContext) -> int:
        ctx.require(Permission.WRITE)
        if not await self._tenancy.tenant_expired(ctx):
            return 0
        return await self._storage.purge_tenant(ctx.org_id, self._options.purge_batch)

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfZwfwYW9oFz2Fn2mVnBK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Jnq1LGkSWCipE7Ap21pyy1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/var/tmp/swe-benchmark/20260930-083846-create-full-system-4bd30619/workspace/0/free_journalism/om/src/free_journalism/om/reports/rules.py","content":""""The reports swimlane's pure rules: the bounds a sealed report, its keys,
and its thread are held to, and the arithmetic of ids and digests the
manager decides by. The platform never reads a report (ADR 0082), so every
rule here is about sizes, shapes, and digests, never about contents."""

import base64
import binascii
import hashlib
import hmac
import re
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

MAX_REPORT_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024
"""The largest sealed report, in bytes of ciphertext: the subject, the
description, the tags, the optional place and time, the optional contact,
and the attachments, all sealed together on the source's device. Sent as
base64 in one JSON body, it is about 6.7 MiB on the wire, which the API
reads whole within a request's deadline."""

MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES = 64 * 1024
"""The largest sealed message of a thread, in bytes of ciphertext: text,
never a file."""

MAX_RECIPIENTS = 10
"""The most journalists one report is sent to at once."""

MAX_WRAPPED_KEY_BYTES = 256
"""A report's key wrapped to one journalist: an ephemeral X25519 public key,
a nonce, the sealed 32-byte key, and its tag come to under a hundred bytes;
the bound leaves room for a format that carries a little more."""

MAX_TAGS = 20
MAX_TAG_LENGTH = 40
"""What a journalist may tag a delivery with: a few short labels of their
own, the one thing the inbox filters by besides the state and the dates."""

_DIGEST = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")


def decoded(value: str, what: str, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    """The bytes a standard base64 string spells, at least one and at most
    `max_bytes` of them; ValueError otherwise."""
    try:
        raw = base64.b64decode(value, validate=True)
    except binascii.Error:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} is standard base64") from None
    if not raw:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} is empty")
    if len(raw) > max_bytes:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} is at most {max_bytes} bytes")
    return raw


def base64_length(max_bytes: int) -> int:
    """How long the standard base64 of `max_bytes` bytes is, padding included:
    the bound a wire field holds the text to before it is decoded."""
    return 4 * -(-max_bytes // 3)


def checked_digest(value: str | None) -> str | None:

    org_id: UUID
    journalist_id: UUID
    delivery_id: UUID

        `NotFound`, one with no public key yet `ValidationFailed`."""

    async def get_deliveries(
        self,
        ctx: TenantContext,
        state: DeliveryState | None,
        tag: str | None,
        after: UUID | None,
        limit: int,
    ) -> DeliveryPage:
        """One page of the desk's inbox, oldest first, strictly after `after`,
        only in `state` and only tagged `tag` when either is given; `limit`
        is clamped."""

    async def get_report(self, ctx: TenantContext, delivery_id: UUID) -> bytes:
        """The sealed report's ciphertext, which only the journalist's own key
        opens. Every open is an audit entry in the desk's stream, naming the
        delivery and the member who opened it, and the entry is appended
        before the bytes are read; the append is a write, so a viewer, whose
        open could leave no entry, opens nothing."""
        ...

    async def create_message(
        self, ctx: TenantContext, delivery_id: UUID, message: Message
    ) -> Message:

        wrote. A delivery whose source gave no key takes no reply
        (`ValidationFailed`). Who wrote it is the stage's."""
        ...

    async def get_messages(

        limit: int,

async def a_journalist(journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl, ctx: TenantContext) -> Journalist:
    now = utcnow()
    return await journalists.create_journalist(
        ctx,
        Journalist(
            id=new_id(),
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
            created_by=ctx.user_id,
            updated_by=ctx.user_id,
            display_name="Ada Reporter",
        ),
    )


def asked(
    journalist_id: UUID,
    amount: int = 1000,
    cadence: SupportCadence = SupportCadence.ONE_TIME,
    support_id: UUID | None = None,
) -> Support:
    """What the service builds from a request: the reader's choice, under the
    id the edge minted, with every field the manager owns left to it."""
    now = utcnow()
    return Support(
        id=support_id or new_id(),
        created_at=now,
        updated_at=now,
        created_by=new_id(),
        updated_by=new_id(),
        version=7,
        journalist_id=journalist_id,
        identity_id=new_id(),
        amount=amount,
        currency="eur",
        cadence=cadence,
        status=SupportStatus.PAID,
        checkout_id="cs_forged",
        checkout_url="https://elsewhere.test",
    )


async def an_open_support(
    support: SupportManagerImpl,
    journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl,
    cadence: SupportCadence = SupportCadence.ONE_TIME,
) -> tuple[TenantContext, IdentityContext, Support]:
    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    reader = visitor()
    made = await support.create_support(reader, desk.org_id, asked(journalist.id, cadence=cadence))
    return desk, reader, made


async def test_a_reader_opens_a_support_and_the_checkout_is_opened_for_it(
    support: SupportManagerImpl,
    journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl,
    twin: PaymentsProviderTwinImpl,
    events: EventStorageMemoryImpl,
) -> None:
    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    reader = visitor()
    made = await support.create_support(
        reader, desk.org_id, asked(journalist.id, 1000, SupportCadence.MONTHLY)
    )
    assert (made.identity_id, made.status, made.version) == (
        reader.identity_id,
        SupportStatus.OPEN,
        2,
    ), "the reader, the status, and the version are the manager's"
    assert (made.created_by, made.updated_by) == (EMPTY_UUID, EMPTY_UUID)
    [(checkout_id, request)] = twin.checkouts.items()
    assert (made.checkout_id, made.checkout_url) == (checkout_id, f"{made.checkout_url}")
    assert made.checkout_url is not None and made.checkout_url.endswith(checkout_id)
    assert (request.reference, request.org_id, request.amount, request.currency) == (
        made.id,
        desk.org_id,
        1000,
        "eur",
    )
    assert request.cadence is Cadence.MONTHLY
    assert request.application_fee == 50, "5% of the amount, the platform's fee"
    back = urlsplit(request.success_url)
    assert f"{back.scheme}://{back.netloc}{back.path}" == RETURN_URL
    assert parse_qs(back.query) == {"support": [str(made.id)], "outcome": ["success"]}
    assert parse_qs(urlsplit(request.cancel_url).query)["outcome"] == ["cancel"]
    assert (await support.get_supports(desk, None, 10)).items == (made,)
    announced = [
        e for e in await events.read_after(desk.org_id, 0, 10) if e.kind.startswith("support")
    ]
    assert [(e.kind, e.target_id, e.actor_id, dict(e.payload)) for e in announced] == [
        ("support.support.created", made.id, EMPTY_UUID, {"version": 1}),
        ("support.support.updated", made.id, EMPTY_UUID, {"version": 2}),
    ], "the announcements name no one: the reader is no user of the desk"


async def test_a_retry_answers_the_same_support_and_opens_no_second_checkout(
    support: SupportManagerImpl, journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl, twin: PaymentsProviderTwinImpl
) -> None:
    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    reader = visitor()
    request = asked(journalist.id)
    first = await support.create_support(reader, desk.org_id, request)
    assert await support.create_support(reader, desk.org_id, request) == first
    assert len(twin.checkouts) == 1
    assert len((await support.get_supports(desk, None, 10)).items) == 1


async def test_a_provider_that_is_down_leaves_the_support_pending_until_a_retry(
    support: SupportManagerImpl,
    journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl,
    twin: PaymentsProviderTwinImpl,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    desk = context(Role.OWNER)
    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    reader = visitor()
    request = asked(journalist.id)

    async def down(_: CheckoutRequest, *, deadline: object = None) -> Checkout:
        raise ProviderUnavailable("the payments provider did not answer")

    monkeypatch.setattr(twin, "open_checkout", down)
    with pytest.raises(Unavailable):
        await support.create_support(reader, desk.org_id, request)
    pending = await support.get_my_support(reader, desk.org_id, request.id)
    assert (pending.status, pending.checkout_url, pending.version) == (
        SupportStatus.PENDING,
        None,
        1,
    )
    monkeypatch.undo()
    opened = await support.create_support(reader, desk.org_id, request)
    assert (opened.id, opened.status, opened.version) == (request.id, SupportStatus.OPEN, 2)
    assert list(twin.checkouts) == [opened.checkout_id]


async def test_a_journalist_the_desk_does_not_hold_cannot_be_supported(
    support: SupportManagerImpl, journalists: JournalistsManagerImpl, twin: PaymentsProviderTwinImpl

    journalist = await a_journalist(journalists, desk)
    with pytest.raises(NotFound):
